verses.transliteration:
uduṣā udu sūrya udidaṃ māmakaṃ vacaḥ |
udejatu prajāpatirvṛṣā śuṣmeṇa vājinā ||

verses.sanskrit:
यथा॑ स्म ते वि॒रोह॑तो॒ऽभित॑प्तमि॒वान॑ति ।
तत॑स्ते॒ शुष्म॑वत्तरमि॒यं कृ॑णो॒त्वोष॑धिः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yathā sma te virohato'bhitaptamivānati |
tataste śuṣmavattaramiyaṃ kṛṇotvoṣadhiḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
उच्छुष्मौष॑धीनां॒ सार॑ ऋष॒भाणा॑म् ।
सं पुं॒सामि॑न्द्र॒ वृष्ण्य॑म॒स्मिन्धे॑हि तनूवशिन् ॥
verses.transliteration:
ucchuṣmauṣadhīnāṃ sāra ṛṣabhāṇām |
saṃ puṃsāmindra vṛṣṇyamasmindhehi tanūvaśin ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒पां रसः॑ प्रथम॒जोऽथो॒ वन॒स्पती॑नाम् ।
उ॒त सोम॑स्य॒ भ्राता॑स्यु॒तार्शम॑सि॒ वृष्ण्य॑म् ॥
verses.transliteration:
apāṃ rasaḥ prathamajo'tho vanaspatīnām |
uta somasya bhrātāsyutārśamasi vṛṣṇyam ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒द्याग्ने॑ अ॒द्य स॑वितर॒द्य दे॑वि सरस्वति ।
अ॑द्यास्य ब्र॑ह्मणस्पते॒ धनु॑रि॒वा ता॑नया॒ पसः॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
adyāgne adya savitaradya devi sarasvati |
adyāsya brahmaṇaspate dhanurivā tānayā pasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
आहं त॑नोमि ते॒ पसो॒ अधि॒ ज्यामि॑व॒ धन्व॑नि ।
क्रम॒स्वर्श॑ इव रो॒हित॒मन॑वग्लायता॒ सदा॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
āhaṃ tanomi te paso adhi jyāmiva dhanvani |
kramasvarśa iva rohitamanavaglāyatā sadā ||

verses.sanskrit:
अश्व॑स्याश्वत॒रस्या॒जस्य॒ पेत्व॑स्य च ।
अथ॑ ऋष॒भस्य॒ ये वाजा॒स्तान॒स्मिन्धे॑हि तनूवशिन् ॥
verses.transliteration:
aśvasyāśvatarasyājasya petvasya ca |
atha ṛṣabhasya ye vājāstānasmindhehi tanūvaśin ||

verses.sanskrit:
स॒हस्र॑शृङ्गो वृष॒भो यः स॑मु॒द्रादु॒दाच॑रत् ।
तेना॑ सह॒स्येऽना व॒यं नि जना॑न्त्स्वापयामसि ॥
verses.transliteration:
sahasraśṛṅgo vṛṣabho yaḥ samudrādudācarat |
tenā sahasye'nā vayaṃ ni janāntsvāpayāmasi ||
verses.translation:
A lover’s sleep-charm
The Bull who hath a thousand horns, who rises up from out the sea,
By him the strong and mighty one we lull the folk to rest and. sleep.
Over the surface of the earth there breathes no wind, there looks. no eye.
Lull all the women, lull the dogs to sleep, with Indra as thy friend!
The woman sleeping in the court, lying without, or stretched on beds,
The matrons with their odorous sweets—these, one and all, we lull to sleep.
Each moving thing have I secured, have held and held the eye and breath.
Each limb and member have I seized in the deep darkness of the night.
The man who sits, the man who walks, whoever stands and clearly sees Of these we closely shut the eyes, even as we closely shut this house.
Sleep mother, let the father sleep, sleep dog, and master of the home.
Let all her kinsmen sleep, sleep all the people who are round about.
With soporific charm, O Sleep, lull thou to slumber all the folk.
Let the rest sleep till break of day, I will remain awake till dawn, like Indra free from scath and harm.

verses.sanskrit:
न भूमिं॒ वातो॒ अति॑ वाति॒ नाति॑ पश्यति॒ कश्च॒न ।
स्त्रिय॑श्च॒ सर्वाः॑ स्वा॒पय॒ शुन॒श्चेन्द्र॑सखा॒ चर॑न् ॥
verses.transliteration:
na bhūmiṃ vāto ati vāti nāti paśyati kaścana |
striyaśca sarvāḥ svāpaya śunaścendrasakhā caran ||

verses.sanskrit:
प्रो॒ष्ठे॒श॒यास्त॑ल्पेश॒या नारी॒र्या व॑ह्य॒शीव॑रीः ।
स्त्रियो॒ याः पुण्य॑गन्धय॒स्ताः सर्वाः॑ स्वापयामसि ॥
verses.transliteration:
proṣṭheśayāstalpeśayā nārīryā vahyaśīvarīḥ |
striyo yāḥ puṇyagandhayastāḥ sarvāḥ svāpayāmasi ||

verses.sanskrit:
एज॑देजदजग्रभं॒ चक्षुः॑ प्रा॒णम॑जग्रभम् ।
अङ्गा॑न्यजग्रभं॒ सर्वा॑ रात्री॑णामतिशर्व॒रे ॥
verses.transliteration:
ejadejadajagrabhaṃ cakṣuḥ prāṇamajagrabham |
aṅgānyajagrabhaṃ sarvā rātrīṇāmatiśarvare ||

verses.sanskrit:
य आस्ते॒ यश्चर॑ति॒ यश्च॒ तिष्ठ॑न्वि॒पश्य॑ति ।
तेषां॒ सं द॑ध्मो॒ अक्षी॑णि॒ यथे॒दं ह॒र्म्यं तथा॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
ya āste yaścarati yaśca tiṣṭhanvipaśyati |
teṣāṃ saṃ dadhmo akṣīṇi yathedaṃ harmyaṃ tathā ||

verses.sanskrit:
स्वप्तु॑ मा॒ता स्वप्तु॑ पि॒ता स्वप्तु॒ श्वा स्वप्तु॑ वि॒श्पतिः॑ ।
स्वप॑न्त्वस्यै ज्ञा॒तयः॒ स्वप्त्व॒यम॒भितो॒ जनः॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
svaptu mātā svaptu pitā svaptu śvā svaptu viśpatiḥ |
svapantvasyai jñātayaḥ svaptvayamabhito janaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
स्वप्न॑ स्वप्नाभि॒कर॑णेन॒ सर्वं॒ नि स्वापया॒ जन॑म् ।
ओ॒त्सू॒र्यम॒न्यान्त्स्वा॒पया॑व्यु॒षं जा॑गृताद॒हमिन्द्र॑ इ॒वारि॑ष्टो॒ अक्षि॑तः ॥
verses.transliteration:
svapna svapnābhikaraṇena sarvaṃ ni svāpayā janam |
otsūryamanyāntsvāpayāvyuṣaṃ jāgṛtādahamindra ivāriṣṭo akṣitaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रा॒ह्म॒णो ज॑ज्ञे प्रथ॒मो दश॑शीर्षो॒ दशा॑स्यः ।
स सोमं॑ प्रथ॒मः प॑पौ॒ स चकारार॒सं वि॒षम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
brāhmaṇo jajñe prathamo daśaśīrṣo daśāsyaḥ |
sa somaṃ prathamaḥ papau sa cakārārasaṃ viṣam ||
verses.translation:
A charm to make a poisoned arrow harmless
The Brāhman first was brought to life ten-headed and with faces ten.
First drinker of the Soma, he made poison ineffectual.
Far as the heavens and earth are spread in compass, far as the Seven Rivers are extended,
So far my spell, the antidote of poison, have I spoken hence,
The strong-winged Bird Garutmān first of all, O Poison fed on thee:
Thou didst not gripe or make him drunk: aye, thou becamest food for him.
Whoever with five fingers hath discharged thee from the crooked bow,
I from the shaft have charmed away the poison of the fastening band.
The poison have I charmed away from shaft, cement, and feather-ed end;
Yea, from the barb, the neck, the horn, the poison have I charmed away.
Feeble, O Arrow, is thy shaft, thy poison, too, hath lost its strength.
Made of a worthless tree, thy bow, O feeble one, is impotent.
The men who brayed it, smeared it on, they who discharged it, sent it forth,
All these are made emasculate, emasculate the poison-hill.
Thy diggers are emasculate, emasculate, O, Plant art thou.
The rugged mountain that produced this poison is emasculate.

verses.sanskrit:
याव॑ती॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी व॑रि॒म्णा यावत् स॒प्त सिन्ध॑वो वितष्ठि॒रे ।
वाचं॑ वि॒षस्य॒ दूष॑णीं॒ तामि॒तो निर॑वादिषम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
yāvatī dyāvāpṛthivī varimṇā yāvat sapta sindhavo vitaṣṭhire |
vācaṃ viṣasya dūṣaṇīṃ tāmito niravādiṣam ||

verses.sanskrit:
सु॒प॒र्णस्त्वा॑ ग॒रुत्मा॒न्विष॑ प्रथ॒ममा॑वयत् ।
नामी॑मदो॒ नारू॑रुप उ॒तास्मा॑ अभवः पि॒तुः ॥
verses.transliteration:
suparṇastvā garutmānviṣa prathamamāvayat |
nāmīmado nārūrupa utāsmā abhavaḥ pituḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
यस्त॒ आस्य॒त् पञ्चा॑ङ्गुरिर्व॒क्राच्चि॒दधि॒ धन्व॑नः ।
अ॒प॒स्क॒म्भस्य॑ श॒ल्यान्निर॑वोचम॒हं वि॒षम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
yasta āsyat pañcāṅgurirvakrāccidadhi dhanvanaḥ |
apaskambhasya śalyānniravocamahaṃ viṣam ||

verses.sanskrit:
श॒ल्याद्वि॒षं निर॑वोचं प्राञ्ज॑नादु॒त प॒र्ण॒धेः ।
अ॒पा॒ष्ठाच्छृङ्गा॒त्कुल्म॑ला॒न्निर॑वोचमहं वि॒ष॑म् ॥
verses.transliteration:
śalyādviṣaṃ niravocaṃ prāñjanāduta parṇadheḥ |
apāṣṭhācchṛṅgātkulmalānniravocamahaṃ viṣam ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒र॒सस्त॑ इषो श॒ल्योऽथो॑ ते अ॒र॒सं वि॒षम् ।
उ॒तार॒सस्य॑ वृ॒क्षस्य॒ धनु॑ष्टे अरसार॒सम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
arasasta iṣo śalyo'tho te arasaṃ viṣam |
utārasasya vṛkṣasya dhanuṣṭe arasārasam ||

verses.sanskrit:
ये अपी॑ष॒न् ये अदि॑ह॒न् य आस्य॒न् ये अ॒वासृ॑जन् ।
सर्वे॒ ते वध्र॑यः कृ॒ता वध्रि॑र्विषगि॒रिः कृतः ॥
verses.transliteration:
ye apīṣan ye adihan ya āsyan ye avāsṛjan |
sarve te vadhrayaḥ kṛtā vadhrirviṣagiriḥ kṛtaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
वध्र॑यस्ते खनि॒तारो॒ वध्रि॒स्त्वम॑स्योषधे ।
वध्रिः॒ स पर्व॑तो गि॒रिर्यतो॑ जा॒तमि॒दं वि॒षम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
vadhrayaste khanitāro vadhristvamasyoṣadhe |
vadhriḥ sa parvato giriryato jātamidaṃ viṣam ||

verses.sanskrit:
वारि॒दं वा॑रयातै वर॒णाव॑त्या॒मधि॑ ।
तत्रा॒मृत॒स्यासि॑क्त॒ तेना॑ ते वारये वि॒षम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
vāridaṃ vārayātai varaṇāvatyāmadhi |
tatrāmṛtasyāsikta tenā te vāraye viṣam ||
verses.translation:
A charm to make a poisonous plant innocuous
So may this water guard us on the bank of Varanāvati.
Therein hath Amrit been infused: with that I ward thy poison off.
Weak is the poison of the East, weak is the poison of the North,
So too this poison of the South counts as a cake of curds and meal.
When he hath made of thee a cake, broad, steaming, swelling up with fat,
And even in hunger eaten thee, then gripe him not, thou hideous one!
Intoxicater! like a shaft we make thy spirit fly away, Like a pot boiling on the fire, we with our word remove thee hence.
We set around thee with the spell as ‘twere a gathered arma-ment.
Stay quiet like a rooted tree. Dug up with mattocks, gripe not thou.
For coverings men have bartered thee, for skins of deer and woven cloths.
Thou art a thing of sale, O Plant. Dug up with mattocks, gripe not thou!
None have attained to those of old, those who wrought holy acts for you.
Let them not harm our heroes here. Therefore I set before you this.

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒र॒सं प्रा॒च्यंऽवि॒षम॑र॒सं यदु॑दी॒च्यऽम् ।
अथे॒दम॑धरा॒च्यं॑ कर॒म्भेण॒ वि क॑ल्पते ॥
verses.transliteration:
arasaṃ prācyaṃ'viṣamarasaṃ yadudīcya'm |
athedamadharācyaṃ karambheṇa vi kalpate ||

verses.sanskrit:
क॒र॒म्भं कृ॒त्वा ति॒र्यंऽपीबस्पा॒कमु॑दार॒थिम् ।
क्षु॒धा किल॑ त्वा दुष्टनो जक्षि॒वान्त्स न रू॑रुपः ॥
verses.transliteration:
karambhaṃ kṛtvā tiryaṃ'pībaspākamudārathim |
kṣudhā kila tvā duṣṭano jakṣivāntsa na rūrupaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
वि ते॒ मदं॑ मदावति श॒रमि॑व पातयामसि ।
प्र त्वा॑ च॒रुमि॑व॒ येष॑न्तं॒ वच॑सा स्थापयामसि ॥
verses.transliteration:
vi te madaṃ madāvati śaramiva pātayāmasi |
pra tvā carumiva yeṣantaṃ vacasā sthāpayāmasi ||

verses.sanskrit:
परि॒ ग्राम॑मि॒वाचि॑तं॒ वच॑सा स्थापयामसि ।
तिष्ठा॑ वृ॒क्ष इ॑व॒ स्थाम्न्यभ्रि॑खाते॒ न रू॑रुपः ॥
verses.transliteration:
pari grāmamivācitaṃ vacasā sthāpayāmasi |
tiṣṭhā vṛkṣa iva sthāmnyabhrikhāte na rūrupaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
प॒वस्तै॑स्त्वा॒ पर्य॑क्रीणन् दू॒र्शेभि॑र॒जिनै॑रु॒त ।
प्र॒क्रीर॑सि॒ त्वमो॑ष॒धेऽभ्रि॑खाते॒ न रू॑रुपः ॥
verses.transliteration:
pavastaistvā paryakrīṇan dūrśebhirajinairuta |
prakrīrasi tvamoṣadhe'bhrikhāte na rūrupaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
अना॑प्ता॒ ये वः॑ प्रथ॒मा यानि॒ कर्मा॑णि चक्रि॒रे॑ ।
वी॒रान्नो॒ अत्र॒ मा द॑भ॒न् तद् व॑ ए॒तत्पु॒रो द॑धे ॥
verses.transliteration:
anāptā ye vaḥ prathamā yāni karmāṇi cakrire |
vīrānno atra mā dabhan tad va etatpuro dadhe ||

verses.sanskrit:
भू॒तो भू॒तेषु॒ पय॒ आ द॑धाति॒ स भू॒ताना॒मधि॑पतिर्बभूव ।
तस्य॑ मृ॒त्युश्च॑रति राज॒सूयं॒ स राजा॑ रा॒ज्यमनु॑ मन्यतामि॒दम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
bhūto bhūteṣu paya ā dadhāti sa bhūtānāmadhipatirbabhūva |
tasya mṛtyuścarati rājasūyaṃ sa rājā rājyamanu manyatāmidam ||
verses.translation:
A benediction at the consecration of a King
The Being lays the sap of life in beings: he hath become the sovran Lord of creatures.
Death comes to this man’s royal consecration: let him as King own and allow this kingdom.
Come forward, turn not back in scorn, strong guardian, slayer of the foes.
Approach, O gladdener of thy friends. The Gods have blessed and strengthened thee.
All waited on him as he came to meet them. He self-resplendent moves endued with glory.
That is the royal hero’s lofty nature: he, manifold, hath gained immortal powers.
Stride forth to heaven’s broad regions, thou, a tiger on a tiger’s skin.
Let all the people long for thee. Let heavenly floods be rich in milk.
Heaven’s waters joyous in their milk, the waters of middle air, and those that earth containethI with the gathered power and might of all these waters sprinkle thee,
The heavenly waters rich in milk have sprinkled thee with power and might.
To be the gladdener of thy friends. May Savitar so fashion thee.
These, compassing the tiger, rouse the lion to great joy and bliss.
As strong floods purify the standing ocean, so men adorn the leopard in the waters

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒भि प्रेहि॒ माप॑ वेन उ॒ग्रश्चे॒त्ता स॑पत्न॒हा ।
आ ति॑ष्ठ मित्रवर्धन॒ तुभ्यं॑ दे॒वा अधि॑ ब्रुवन् ॥
verses.transliteration:
abhi prehi māpa vena ugraścettā sapatnahā |
ā tiṣṭha mitravardhana tubhyaṃ devā adhi bruvan ||

verses.sanskrit:
आ॒तिष्ठ॑न्तं॒ परि॒ विश्वे॑ अभूषं॒छ्रियं॒ वसा॑नश्चरति॒ स्वरो॑चिः ।
म॒हत् तद् वृष्णो॒ असु॑रस्य॒ नामा वि॒श्वरू॑पो अ॒मृता॑नि तस्थौ ॥
verses.transliteration:
ātiṣṭhantaṃ pari viśve abhūṣaṃchriyaṃ vasānaścarati svarociḥ |
mahat tad vṛṣṇo asurasya nāmā viśvarūpo amṛtāni tasthau ||

verses.sanskrit:
व्या॒घ्रो अधि॒ वैया॑घ्रे॒ वि क्र॑मस्व॒ दिशो॑ म॒हीः ।
विश॑स्त्वा॒ सर्वा॑ वाञ्छ॒न्त्वापो॑ दिव्याः पय॑स्वतीः ॥
verses.transliteration:
vyāghro adhi vaiyāghre vi kramasva diśo mahīḥ |
viśastvā sarvā vāñchantvāpo divyāḥ payasvatīḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
या आपो॑ दि॒व्याः पय॑सा॒ मद॑न्त्य॒न्तरि॑क्ष उ॒त वा॑ पृथि॒व्याम् ।
तासां॑ त्वा॒ सर्वा॑साम॒पाम॒भि॑ षि॑ञ्चामि॒ वर्च॑सा ॥
verses.transliteration:
yā āpo divyāḥ payasā madantyantarikṣa uta vā pṛthivyām |
tāsāṃ tvā sarvāsāmapāmabhi ṣiñcāmi varcasā ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒भि त्वा॒ वर्च॑सासिच॒न्नापो॑ दि॒व्याः पय॑स्वतीः ।
यथासो॑ मित्र॒वर्ध॑न॒स्तथा॑ त्वा सवि॒ता क॑रत् ॥
verses.transliteration:
abhi tvā varcasāsicannāpo divyāḥ payasvatīḥ |
yathāso mitravardhanastathā tvā savitā karat ||

verses.sanskrit:
ए॒ना व्या॒घ्रं प॑रिषस्वजा॒नाः सिं॒हं हि॑न्वन्ति मह॒ते सौभ॑गाय ।
स॒मु॒द्रं न सु॒भुव॑स्तस्थि॒वांसं॑ मर्मृ॒ज्यन्ते॑ द्वी॒पिन॑म॒प्स्व॑१न्तः ॥
verses.transliteration:
enā vyāghraṃ pariṣasvajānāḥ siṃhaṃ hinvanti mahate saubhagāya |
samudraṃ na subhuvastasthivāṃsaṃ marmṛjyante dvīpinamapsvantaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
एहि॑ जी॒वं त्राय॑माणं॒ पर्व॑तस्या॒स्यक्ष्य॑म् ।
विश्वे॑भिर्दे॒वैर्द॒त्तं प॑रि॒धिर्जीव॑नाय॒ कम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
ehi jīvaṃ trāyamāṇaṃ parvatasyāsyakṣyam |
viśvebhirdevairdattaṃ paridhirjīvanāya kam ||
verses.translation:
A charm addressed to a precious ointment for safety and wealth
Approach! thou art the mountain’s eye, the living thing that saveth us;
A gift bestowed by all the Gods, yea, the defence that guardeth life.
Thou art the safeguard of the men, thou art the safeguard of the kine,
Thou standest ready to protect the horses that are fleet of foot.
Thou, also, Salve! art a defence that rends and crushes sorcerers.
Thou knowest, too, of Amrit, thou art the delight of all who live, a jaundice-curing balm art thou.
Whomso thou creepest over, Salve! member by member, joint by joint,
From him, like some strong arbiter of strife, thou banishest decline.
No imprecation reaches him, no magic, no tormenting fiend,
O Salve, Vishkandha seizes not the man who carries thee about.
From lying speech, from evil dream, from wicked act and sinfulness,
From hostile and malignant eye,—from these, O Salve, protect us well.
I, knowing this, O Salve, will speak the very truth and not a lie:
May I obtain both horse and ox, may I obtain thy life, O man.
Three are the slaves that serve the Salve, Fever, Consumption, and the Snake.
Thy father is the loftiest of mountains, named the Triple-peaked.
Sprung from the Snowy Mountain’s side, this Ointment of the Three-peaked hill.
Crushes and rends all sorcerers and every witch and sorceress.
If thou art from the Three-peaked hill or hast thy name from Yamunā,
These names are both auspicious: by these two protect thou us,
O Salve!

verses.sanskrit:
प॒रि॒पाणं॒ पुरु॑षाणां परि॒पाणं॒ गवा॑मसि ।
अश्वा॑ना॒मर्व॑तां परि॒पाणा॑य तस्थिषे ॥
verses.transliteration:
paripāṇaṃ puruṣāṇāṃ paripāṇaṃ gavāmasi |
aśvānāmarvatāṃ paripāṇāya tasthiṣe ||

verses.sanskrit:
उ॒तासि॑ परि॒पाणं॑ यातु॒जम्भ॑नमाञ्जन ।
उ॒तामृत॑स्य॒ त्वं वे॒त्थाथो॑ असि जीव॒भोज॑न॒मथो॑ हरितभेष॒जम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
utāsi paripāṇaṃ yātujambhanamāñjana |
utāmṛtasya tvaṃ vetthātho asi jīvabhojanamatho haritabheṣajam ||

verses.sanskrit:
यस्या॑ञ्जन प्र॒सर्प॒स्यङ्ग॑मङ्गं॒ परु॑ष्परुः ।
ततो॒ यक्ष्मं॒ वि बा॑धस उ॒ग्रो मध्यम॒शीरि॑व ॥
verses.transliteration:
yasyāñjana prasarpasyaṅgamaṅgaṃ paruṣparuḥ |
tato yakṣmaṃ vi bādhasa ugro madhyamaśīriva ||

verses.sanskrit:
नैनं॒ प्राप्नो॑ति श॒पथो॒ न कृ॒त्या नाभि॒शोच॑नम् ।
नैनं॒ विष्क॑न्धमश्नुते॒ यस्त्वा॒ बिभ॑र्त्याञ्जन ॥
verses.transliteration:
nainaṃ prāpnoti śapatho na kṛtyā nābhiśocanam |
nainaṃ viṣkandhamaśnute yastvā bibhartyāñjana ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒स॒न्म॒न्त्रा॑द् दु॒ष्वप्न्याद् दुष्कृ॒ताच्छम॑लादु॒त ।
दु॒र्हार्द॒श्चक्षु॑षो घो॒रात् तस्मा॑न्नः पाह्याञ्जन ॥
verses.transliteration:
asanmantrād duṣvapnyād duṣkṛtācchamalāduta |
durhārdaścakṣuṣo ghorāt tasmānnaḥ pāhyāñjana ||

verses.sanskrit:
इ॒दं वि॒द्वाना॑ञ्जन स॒त्यं व॑क्ष्यामि॒ नानृ॑तम् ।
स॒नेय॒मश्वं॒ गाम॒हमा॒त्मानं॒ तव॒ पूरुष ॥
verses.transliteration:
idaṃ vidvānāñjana satyaṃ vakṣyāmi nānṛtam |
saneyamaśvaṃ gāmahamātmānaṃ tava pūruṣa ||

verses.sanskrit:
त्रयो॑ दा॒सा आञ्ज॑नस्य त॒क्मा ब॒लास॒ आदहिः॑ ।
वर्षि॑ष्ठः॒ पर्व॑तानां त्रिक॒कुन्नाम॑ ते पि॒ता ॥
verses.transliteration:
trayo dāsā āñjanasya takmā balāsa ādahiḥ |
varṣiṣṭhaḥ parvatānāṃ trikakunnāma te pitā ||

verses.sanskrit:
यदाञ्ज॑नं त्रैककु॒दं जा॒तं हि॒मव॑त॒स्परि॑ ।
या॒तूंश्च॒ सर्वा॑ञ्ज॒म्भय॒त् सर्वा॑श्च यातुधा॒न्यः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yadāñjanaṃ traikakudaṃ jātaṃ himavataspari |
yātūṃśca sarvāñjambhayat sarvāśca yātudhānyaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
यदि॒ वासि॑ त्रैककु॒दं यदि॑ यामु॒नमु॒च्यसे॑ ।
उ॒भे ते॑ भ॒द्रे॑ नाम्नी॒ ताभ्यां॒ नः पाह्याञ्जन ॥
verses.transliteration:
yadi vāsi traikakudaṃ yadi yāmunamucyase |
ubhe te bhadre nāmnī tābhyāṃ naḥ pāhyāñjana ||

verses.sanskrit:
वाता॑ज्जा॒तो अ॒न्तरि॑क्षाद् वि॒द्युतो॒ ज्योति॑ष॒स्परि ।
स नो॑ हिरण्य॒जाः श॒ङ्खः कृश॑नः पा॒त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
vātājjāto antarikṣād vidyuto jyotiṣaspari |
sa no hiraṇyajāḥ śaṅkhaḥ kṛśanaḥ pātvaṃhasaḥ ||
verses.translation:
A charm accompanying investiture with an amulet of shell
Child of the wind firmament, sprung from the lightning and the light,
May this the gold-born Shell that bears the pearl preserve us from distress.
Shell that wast born from out the sea, set at the head of things that shine!
With thee we slay the Rākshasas and overcome voracious fiends.
We stay disease and indigence, and chase Sadānvās with the Shell.
May the all-healing Shell that bears the pearl preserve us from distress.
Born in the heaven, sprung from the sea, brought to us hither from the flood.
This gold-born Shell shall be to us an amulet to lengthen life.
From ocean sprang the Amulet, from Vritra sprang the Lord of Day:
May this protect us round about from shaft of God and Asura.
Peerless ‘mid golden ornaments art thou: from Soma wast thou born.
Thou gleamest on the quiver, thou art beautiful upon the car: may it prolong our days of life!
Bone of the Good became the pearl’s shell-mother endowed with soul it moveth in the waters.
I bind this on thee for life, strength, and vigour, for long life lasting through a hundred autumns.
May the pearl’s mother keep and guard thee safely!

verses.sanskrit:
यो अ॑ग्र॒तो रो॑च॒नानां॑ समु॒द्रादधि॑ जज्ञि॒षे ।
श॒ङ्खेन॑ ह॒त्वा रक्षां॑स्य॒त्त्रिणो॒ वि ष॑हामहे ॥
verses.transliteration:
yo agrato rocanānāṃ samudrādadhi jajñiṣe |
śaṅkhena hatvā rakṣāṃsyattriṇo vi ṣahāmahe ||

verses.sanskrit:
श॒ङ्खेनामी॑वा॒मम॑तिं श॒ङ्खेनो॒त सदान्वाः॑ ।
श॒ङ्खो नो॑ वि॒श्वभे॑षजः॒ कृश॑नः पा॒त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
śaṅkhenāmīvāmamatiṃ śaṅkhenota sadānvāḥ |
śaṅkho no viśvabheṣajaḥ kṛśanaḥ pātvaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
दि॒वि जा॒तः स॑मुद्र॒जः सि॑न्धु॒तस्पर्याभृ॑तः ।
स नो॑ हिरण्य॒जाः श॒ङ्ख आ॑युष्प्र॒तर॑णो म॒णिः ॥
verses.transliteration:
divi jātaḥ samudrajaḥ sindhutasparyābhṛtaḥ |
sa no hiraṇyajāḥ śaṅkha āyuṣprataraṇo maṇiḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
स॒मु॒द्राज्जा॒तो म॒णिर्वृ॒त्राज्जा॒तो दि॑वाक॒रः ।
सो अ॒स्मान्त्स॒र्वतः॑ पातु हे॒त्या दे॑वासु॒रेभ्यः॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
samudrājjāto maṇirvṛtrājjāto divākaraḥ |
so asmāntsarvataḥ pātu hetyā devāsurebhyaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
हिर॑ण्याना॒मेको॑ऽसि॒ सोमा॒त् त्वमधि॑ जज्ञिषे ।
रथे॒ त्वम॑सि दर्श॒त॑ इ॑षु॒धौ रो॑च॒नस्त्वं प्र ण॒ आयूं॑षि तारिषत् ॥
verses.transliteration:
hiraṇyānāmeko'si somāt tvamadhi jajñiṣe |
rathe tvamasi darśata iṣudhau rocanastvaṃ pra ṇa āyūṃṣi tāriṣat ||

verses.sanskrit:
दे॒वाना॒मस्थि॒ कृश॑नं बभूव॒ तदा॑त्म॒न्वच्च॑रत्य॒प्स्व॑१न्तः ।
तत् ते॑ बध्ना॒म्यायु॑षे॒ वर्च॑से॒ बला॑य दीर्घायु॒त्वाय॑ श॒तशा॑रदाय कार्श॒नस्त्वा॒भि र॑क्षतु ॥
verses.transliteration:
devānāmasthi kṛśanaṃ babhūva tadātmanvaccaratyapsvantaḥ |
tat te badhnāmyāyuṣe varcase balāya dīrghāyutvāya śataśāradāya kārśanastvābhi rakṣatu ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒न॒ड्वान् दा॑धार पृथि॒वीमु॒त द्याम॑न॒ड्वान् दा॑धारो॒र्व१न्तरि॑क्षम् ।
अ॒न॒ड्वान् दा॑धार प्र॒दिशः॒ षडु॒र्वीर॑न॒ड्वान् विश्वं॒ भुव॑न॒मा वि॑वेश ॥
verses.transliteration:
anaḍvān dādhāra pṛthivīmuta dyāmanaḍvān dādhārorvantarikṣam |
anaḍvān dādhāra pradiśaḥ ṣaḍurvīranaḍvān viśvaṃ bhuvanamā viveśa ||
verses.translation:
A glorification of the sacrificial gharma or milk caldron
The Bull supports the wide-spread earth and heaven, the Bull supports the spacious air between them.
The Bull supports the sky’s six spacious regions: the universal world hath he pervaded.
The Bull is Indra o’er the beasts he watches. He, Sakra measures out three several pathways.
He, milking out the worlds, the past, the future, discharges all the Gods’ eternal duties.
Being produced among mankind as Indra, the Caldron works heated and brightly glowing.
Let him not, with good sons, pass off in vapour who hath not eaten of the Ox with knowledge.
The Ox pours milk out in the world of virtue: in earliest time, he, Pavamna, swells it.
Parjanya is the stream, Maruts his udder, sacrifice is the milk, the meed his milking.
That which not sacrifice nor sacrificer, not giver nor receiver rules and governs,
All-winning, all-supporting, all-effecting,—which of all quadru-peds, tell us! is the Caldron?
May we, fame-seekers, reach the world of virtue by service of the Gharma and through fervour,
Whereby the Gods went up to heaven, the centre of life eternal, having left the body.
Prajāpati, supreme and sovran ruler, Indra by form and by his shoulder Agni,
Came to Visvānara, came to all men’s Bullock: he firmly forti-fied and held securely.
The middle of the Bullock’s neck, there where the shoulder-bar is placed,
Extends as far to east of him as that is settled to the west.
He whosoever knows the seven exhaustless pourings of the Ox,
Wins himself offspring and the world: the great Seven Rishis know this well.
With feet subduing weariness, with legs extracting freshening draughts,
Through toil the plougher and the Ox approach the honeyed beverage.
Assigned are these twelve nights, they say, as holy to Prajāpati:
Whoever knows their proper prayer performs the service of the Ox.
At evening he is milked, is milked at early morn, is milked at noon.
We know that streams of milk that flow from him are in-exhaustible.

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒न॒ड्वानिन्द्रः॒ स प॒शुभ्यो॒ वि च॑ष्टे त्र॒यां छ॒क्रो वि मि॑मीते॒ अध्व॑नः ।
भू॒तं भ॑वि॒ष्यद् भुव॑ना॒ दुहा॑नः॒ सर्वा॑ दे॒वानां॑ चरति व्र॒तानि॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
anaḍvānindraḥ sa paśubhyo vi caṣṭe trayāṃ chakro vi mimīte adhvanaḥ |
bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyad bhuvanā duhānaḥ sarvā devānāṃ carati vratāni ||

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रो॑ जा॒तो म॑नु॒ष्येऽष्व॒न्तर्घ॒र्मस्त॒प्तश्च॑रति॒ शोशु॑चानः ।
सु॒प्र॒जाः सन्त्स उ॑दा॒रे न स॑र्ष॒द्यो नाश्नी॒यादन॒डुहो॑ विजा॒नन् ॥
verses.transliteration:
indro jāto manuṣye'ṣvantargharmastaptaścarati śośucānaḥ |
suprajāḥ santsa udāre na sarṣadyo nāśnīyādanaḍuho vijānan ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒न॒ड्वान् दु॑हे सुकृ॒तस्य॑ लो॒क ऐनं॑ प्याययति॒ पव॑मानः पु॒रस्ता॑त् ।
प॒र्जन्यो॒ धारा॑ म॒रुत॒ ऊधो॑ अस्य य॒ज्ञः पयो॒ दक्षि॑णा॒ दोहो॑ अस्य ॥
verses.transliteration:
anaḍvān duhe sukṛtasya loka ainaṃ pyāyayati pavamānaḥ purastāt |
parjanyo dhārā maruta ūdho asya yajñaḥ payo dakṣiṇā doho asya ||

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य॒ नेशे॑ य॒ज्ञप॑ति॒र्न य॒ज्ञो नास्य॑ दा॒तेशे॒ न प्र॑तिग्रही॒ता ।
यो वि॑श्व॒जिद् वि॑श्व॒भृद् वि॒श्क॑र्मा घ॒र्मं नो॑ ब्रूत यत॒मश्चतु॑ष्पात् ॥
verses.transliteration:
yasya neśe yajñapatirna yajño nāsya dāteśe na pratigrahītā |
yo viśvajid viśvabhṛd viśkarmā gharmaṃ no brūta yatamaścatuṣpāt ||

verses.sanskrit:
येन॑ दे॒वाः स्वरारुरु॒हुर्हि॒त्वा शरी॑रम॒मृत॑स्य॒ नाभि॑म् ।
तेन॑ गेष्म सुकृ॒तस्य॑ लो॒कं घ॒र्मस्य॑ व्र॒तेन॒ तप॑सा यश॒स्यवः॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
yena devāḥ svarāruruhurhitvā śarīramamṛtasya nābhim |
tena geṣma sukṛtasya lokaṃ gharmasya vratena tapasā yaśasyavaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रो॑ रू॒पेणा॒ग्निर्वहे॑न प्र॒जाप॑तिः परमे॒ष्ठी वि॒राट् ।
वि॒श्वान॑रे अक्रमत वैश्वान॒रे अ॑क्रमतान॒दुह्य॑क्रमत । सोऽदृंहयत॒ सोऽधारयत ॥
verses.transliteration:
indro rūpeṇāgnirvahena prajāpatiḥ parameṣṭhī virāṭ |
viśvānare akramata vaiśvānare akramatānaduhyakramata | so'dṛṃhayata so'dhārayata ||

verses.sanskrit:
मध्य॑मे॒तद॑न॒डुहो॒ यत्रै॒ष वह॒ आहि॑तः ।
ए॒ताव॑दस्य प्रा॒चीनं॒ यावा॑न् प्र॒त्यङ् स॒माहि॑तः ॥
verses.transliteration:
madhyametadanaḍuho yatraiṣa vaha āhitaḥ |
etāvadasya prācīnaṃ yāvān pratyaṅ samāhitaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
यो वेदा॑न॒डुहो॒ दोहा॑न्त्स॒प्तानु॑पदस्वतः ।
प्र॒जां च॑ लो॒कं चा॑प्नोति॒ तथा॑ सप्तऋ॒षयो॑ विदुः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yo vedānaḍuho dohāntsaptānupadasvataḥ |
prajāṃ ca lokaṃ cāpnoti tathā saptaṛṣayo viduḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
प॒द्भिः से॒दिम॑व॒क्राम॒न्निरां॒ जङ्घा॑भिरुत्खि॒दन् ।
श्रमे॑णान॒ड्वान् की॒लालं॑ की॒नाश॑श्चाभि ग॑च्छतः ॥
verses.transliteration:
padbhiḥ sedimavakrāmannirāṃ jaṅghābhirutkhidan |
śrameṇānaḍvān kīlālaṃ kīnāśaścābhi gacchataḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
द्वाद॑श॒ वा ए॒ता रात्री॒र्व्रत्या॑ आहुः प्र॒जाप॑तेः ।
तत्रोप॒ ब्रह्म॒ यो वेद॒ तद् वा अ॑न॒डुहो॑ व्र॒तम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
dvādaśa vā etā rātrīrvratyā āhuḥ prajāpateḥ |
tatropa brahma yo veda tad vā anaḍuho vratam ||

verses.sanskrit:
दु॒हे सा॒यं दु॒हे प्रा॒तर्दु॒हे म॒ध्यंदि॑नं॒ परि॑ ।
दोहा॒ ये अ॑स्य सं॒यन्ति॒ ता॑न् वि॒द्मानु॑पदस्वतः ॥
verses.transliteration:
duhe sāyaṃ duhe prātarduhe madhyaṃdinaṃ pari |
dohā ye asya saṃyanti tān vidmānupadasvataḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
रोह॑ण्यसि॒ रोह॑ण्य॒स्थ्नश्छि॒न्नस्य॒ रोह॑णी ।
रो॒हये॒दम॑रुन्धति ॥
verses.transliteration:
rohaṇyasi rohaṇyasthnaśchinnasya rohaṇī |
rohayedamarundhati ||
verses.translation:
A charm to mend a broken bone
Thou art the healer, making whole, the healer of the broken bone:
Make thou this whole, Arundhatī!
Whatever bone of thine within thy body hath been wrenched or cracked,
May Dhātar set it properly and join together limb by limb.
With marrow be the marrow joined, thy limb united with the limb.
Let what hath fallen of thy flesh, and the bone also grow again.
Let marrow close with marrow, let skin grow united with the skin.
Let blood and bone grow strong in thee, flesh grow together with the flesh.
Join thou together hair with hair, join thou together skin with skin.
Let blood and bone grow strong in thee. Unite the broken part,.
O Plant.
Arise, advance, speed forth; the car hath goodly fellies, naves, and wheels!!
Stand up erect upon thy feet.
If he be torn and shattered, having fallen into a pit, or a cast stone have struck him,
Let the skilled leech join limb with limb, as ‘twere the portions of a car.

verses.sanskrit:
यत् ते॑ रि॒ष्टं य॑त् ते द्यु॒त्तमस्ति॒ पेष्ट्रं॑ त आ॒त्मनि ।
धा॒ता तद् भ॒द्रया॒ पुनः॒ सं द॑ध॒त् परु॑षा॒ परुः॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
yat te riṣṭaṃ yat te dyuttamasti peṣṭraṃ ta ātmani |
dhātā tad bhadrayā punaḥ saṃ dadhat paruṣā paruḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
सं ते॑ म॒ज्जा म॒ज्ज्ञा भ॑वतु॒ समु॑ ते॒ परु॑षा॒ परुः॑ ।
सं ते॑ मां॒सस्य॒ विस्र॑स्तं॒ समस्थ्यपि॑ रोहतु ॥
verses.transliteration:
saṃ te majjā majjñā bhavatu samu te paruṣā paruḥ |
saṃ te māṃsasya visrastaṃ samasthyapi rohatu ||

verses.sanskrit:
म॒ज्जा म॒ज्ज्ञा सं धी॑यतां॒ चर्म॑णा॒ चर्म॑ रोहतु ।
असृ॑क् ते॒ अस्थि॑ रोहतु मां॒सं मां॒सेन॑ रोहतु ॥
verses.transliteration:
majjā majjñā saṃ dhīyatāṃ carmaṇā carma rohatu |
asṛk te asthi rohatu māṃsaṃ māṃsena rohatu ||

verses.sanskrit:
लोम॒ लोम्ना॒ सं क॑ल्पया त्व॒चा सं क॑ल्पया॒ त्वच॑म् ।
असृ॑क् ते॒ अस्थि॑ रोहतु छि॒न्नं सं धे॑ह्योषधे ॥
verses.transliteration:
loma lomnā saṃ kalpayā tvacā saṃ kalpayā tvacam |
asṛk te asthi rohatu chinnaṃ saṃ dhehyoṣadhe ||

verses.sanskrit:
स उत् ति॑ष्ठ॒ प्रेहि॒ प्र द्र॑व॒ रथः॑ सुच॒क्रः सु॑प॒विः सु॒नाभिः॑ ।
प्रति॑ तिष्ठो॒र्ध्वः ॥
verses.transliteration:
sa ut tiṣṭha prehi pra drava rathaḥ sucakraḥ supaviḥ sunābhiḥ |
prati tiṣṭhordhvaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
यदि॑ क॒र्तं प॑ति॒त्वा सं॑श॒श्रे यदि॒ वाश्मा॒ प्रहृ॑तो ज॒घान॑ ।
ऋ॒भू रथ॑स्ये॒वाङ्गा॑नि॒ सं द॑ध॒त् परु॑षा॒ परुः॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
yadi kartaṃ patitvā saṃśaśre yadi vāśmā prahṛto jaghāna |
ṛbhū rathasyevāṅgāni saṃ dadhat paruṣā paruḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
उ॒त दे॑वा॒ अव॑हितं॒ देवा॒ उन्न॑यथा॒ पुनः॑ ।
उ॒ताग॑श्च॒क्रुषं॑ देवा॒ देवा॑ जी॒वय॑था॒ पुनः॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
uta devā avahitaṃ devā unnayathā punaḥ |
utāgaścakruṣaṃ devā devā jīvayathā punaḥ ||
verses.translation:
A charm to restore a sick man to health
Gods, raise again the man whom ye, O Gods, have humbled and brought low.
Ye Gods, restore to life again, him, Gods! who hath committed sin.
Here these two winds are blowing far as Sindhu from a distant land.
May one breathe energy to thee, the other blow thy fault away.
Hither, O Wind, blow healing balm, blow every fault away, thou Wind!
For thou who hast all medicine comest as envoy of the Gods.
May the Gods keep and save this man, the Maruts’ host deliver him.
All things that be deliver him that he be freed from his offence.
I am come nigh to thee with balms to give thee rest and keep thee safe.
I bring thee mighty strength, I drive thy wasting malady away.
Felicitous is this my hand, yet more felicitous is this.
This hand contains all healing balms, and this makes whole with gentle touch.
The tongue that leads the voice precedes. Then with our tenfold-branching hands.
With these two healers of disease, we stroke thee with a soft caress.

verses.sanskrit:
द्वावि॒मौ वातौ॒ वात॒ आ सिन्धो॒रा प॑रावतः॑ ।
दक्षं॑ ते अ॒न्य आ॒वातु॒ व्य॑१न्यो वा॑तु॒ यद् रपः॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
dvāvimau vātau vāta ā sindhorā parāvataḥ |
dakṣaṃ te anya āvātu vyanyo vātu yad rapaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
आ वा॑त वाहि भेष॒जं वि वा॑त वाहि॒ यद्रपः॑ ।
त्वं हि वि॑श्वभेषज दे॒वानां॑ दू॒त ईय॑से ॥
verses.transliteration:
ā vāta vāhi bheṣajaṃ vi vāta vāhi yadrapaḥ |
tvaṃ hi viśvabheṣaja devānāṃ dūta īyase ||

verses.sanskrit:
त्राय॑न्तामि॒मं दे॒वास्त्राय॑न्तां म॒रुतां॑ ग॒णाः ।
त्राय॑न्तां॒ विश्वा॑ भू॒तानि॒ यथा॒यम॑र॒पा अस॑त् ॥
verses.transliteration:
trāyantāmimaṃ devāstrāyantāṃ marutāṃ gaṇāḥ |
trāyantāṃ viśvā bhūtāni yathāyamarapā asat ||

verses.sanskrit:
आ त्वा॑गमं॒ शंता॑तिभि॒रथो॑ अरि॒ष्टता॑तिभिः ।
दक्षं॑ त उ॒ग्रमाभा॑रिषं॒ परा॒ यक्ष्मं॑ सुवामि ते ॥
verses.transliteration:
ā tvāgamaṃ śaṃtātibhiratho ariṣṭatātibhiḥ |
dakṣaṃ ta ugramābhāriṣaṃ parā yakṣmaṃ suvāmi te ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒यं मे॒ हस्तो॒ भग॑वान॒यं मे॒ भग॑वत्तरः ।
अ॒यं मे॑ वि॒श्वभे॑षजो॒ऽयं शि॒वाभि॑मर्शनः ॥
verses.transliteration:
ayaṃ me hasto bhagavānayaṃ me bhagavattaraḥ |
ayaṃ me viśvabheṣajo'yaṃ śivābhimarśanaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
हस्ता॑भ्यां॒ दश॑शाखाभ्यां जि॒ह्वा वा॒चः पु॑रोग॒वी ।
अ॒ना॒म॒यि॒त्नुभ्यां॒ हस्ता॑भ्यां॒ ताभ्यां॑ त्वा॒भि मृ॑शामसि ॥
verses.transliteration:
hastābhyāṃ daśaśākhābhyāṃ jihvā vācaḥ purogavī |
anāmayitnubhyāṃ hastābhyāṃ tābhyāṃ tvābhi mṛśāmasi ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒जो ह्य॑१ग्नेरज॑निष्ट॒ शोका॒त् सो अ॑पश्यज्जनि॒तार॒मग्रे॑ ।
तेन॑ दे॒वा दे॒वता॒मग्रा॑ आय॒न् तेन॒ रोहा॑न् रुरुहु॒र्मेध्या॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
ajo hyagnerajaniṣṭa śokāt so apaśyajjanitāramagre |
tena devā devatāmagrā āyan tena rohān ruruhurmedhyāsaḥ ||
verses.translation:
Accompanying the sacrifice of a he-goat
The Goat was verily produced from Agni. Through sorrow he beheld, at first, his father.
Through him at first the Gods attained to godhead, and, meet for sacrifices, were exalted.
Bearing in hands seethed viands, go with Agni to the cope of heaven.
Reaching the sky that touches heaven, mix with the company of Gods.
From earth’s high ridge to middle air I mounted, and from mid-air ascended up to heaven.
From the high pitch of heaven’s cope I came into the world of light.
Mounting the sky they look not round; they rise to heaven through both the worlds,
Sages who paid the sacrifice that pours its streams on every side.
First among all the deities, come forward, thou who art eye of Gods and men, O Agni.
Imploring, and accordant with the Bhrigus, to heaven in safety go the sacrificers!
With milk and butter I anoint the mighty, celestial Goat, strong-winged, and full of juices.
Through him will we attain the world of virtue, ascending to the loftiest cope, to heaven.
Set the Goat’s head toward the eastern region, and turn his right side to the southern quarter.
His hinder part turn to the western quarter, and set his left side to the northern region.
Set the Goat’s backbone upmost in the zenith, and lay his belly downward in the nadir; set his midportion in mid-air between them.
O’er the dressed Goat lay a dressed skin to robe him prepared, in perfect form, with all his members.
Rise upward to the loftiest vault of heaven: with thy four feet stand firmly in the regions.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रम॑ध्वम॒ग्निना॒ नाक॒मुख्या॒न् हस्ते॑षु॒ बिभ्र॑तः ।
दि॒वस्पृ॒ष्ठं स्वऽर्ग॒त्वा मि॒श्रा दे॒वेभि॑राध्वम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
kramadhvamagninā nākamukhyān hasteṣu bibhrataḥ |
divaspṛṣṭhaṃ sva'rgatvā miśrā devebhirādhvam ||

verses.sanskrit:
पृ॒ष्ठात् पृ॑थि॒व्या अ॒हम॒न्तरि॑क्ष॒मारु॑हम॒न्तरि॑क्षा॒द् दिव॒मारु॑हम् ।
दि॒वो नाक॑स्य पृ॒ष्ठात् स्व॑१र्ज्योति॑रगाम॒हम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
pṛṣṭhāt pṛthivyā ahamantarikṣamāruhamantarikṣād divamāruham |
divo nākasya pṛṣṭhāt svarjyotiragāmaham ||

verses.sanskrit:
स्व॑१र्यन्तो॒ नापे॑क्षन्त॒ आ द्यां रो॑हन्ति॒ रोद॑सी ।
य॒ज्ञं ये वि॒श्वतो॑धारं॒ सुवि॑द्वांसो वितेनि॒रे ॥
verses.transliteration:
svaryanto nāpekṣanta ā dyāṃ rohanti rodasī |
yajñaṃ ye viśvatodhāraṃ suvidvāṃso vitenire ||

verses.sanskrit:
अग्ने॒ प्रेहि॑ प्रथ॒मो दे॒वता॑नां॒ चक्षु॑र्दे॒वाना॑मु॒त मानु॑षानाम् ।
इय॑क्षमाणा॒ भृगु॑भिः स॒जोषाः॒ स्वऽर्यन्तु॒ यज॑मानाः स्व॒स्ति ॥
verses.transliteration:
agne prehi prathamo devatānāṃ cakṣurdevānāmuta mānuṣānām |
iyakṣamāṇā bhṛgubhiḥ sajoṣāḥ sva'ryantu yajamānāḥ svasti ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒जम॑नज्मि॒ पय॑सा घृ॒तेन॑ दि॒व्यं सु॑प॒र्नं प॑य॒सं बृ॒हन्त॑म् ।
तेन॑ गेष्म सुकृ॒तस्य॑ लो॒कं स्वऽरा॒रोह॑न्तो अ॒भि नाक॑मुत्त॒मम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
ajamanajmi payasā ghṛtena divyaṃ suparnaṃ payasaṃ bṛhantam |
tena geṣma sukṛtasya lokaṃ sva'rārohanto abhi nākamuttamam ||

verses.sanskrit:
पञ्चौ॑दनं प॒ञ्चभि॑र॒ङ्गुलि॑भि॒र्द॑र्व्योद्ध॑र पञ्च॒धैतमो॑द॒नम् ।
प्राच्यां॑ दि॒शि शिरो॑ अ॒जस्य॑ धेहि॒ दक्षि॑णायां दि॒शि दक्षि॑णं धेहि पा॒र्श्वम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
pañcaudanaṃ pañcabhiraṅgulibhirdarvyoddhara pañcadhaitamodanam |
prācyāṃ diśi śiro ajasya dhehi dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśi dakṣiṇaṃ dhehi pārśvam ||

verses.sanskrit:
प्र॒तीच्यां॑ दि॒शि भ॒सद॒मस्य धेह्युत्त॑रस्यां दि॒श्युत्त॑रं धेहि पा॒र्श्वम् ।
ऊ॒र्ध्वायां॑ दि॒श्य॑१जस्यानू॑कं धेहि दि॒शि ध्रु॒वायां॑ धेहि पाज॒स्यऽम॒न्तरि॑क्षे मध्य॒तो मध्य॑मस्य ॥
verses.transliteration:
pratīcyāṃ diśi bhasadamasya dhehyuttarasyāṃ diśyuttaraṃ dhehi pārśvam |
ūrdhvāyāṃ diśyajasyānūkaṃ dhehi diśi dhruvāyāṃ dhehi pājasya'mantarikṣe madhyato madhyamasya ||

verses.sanskrit:
शृ॒तम॒जं शृ॒तया॒ प्रोर्णु॑हि त्व॒चा सर्वै॒रङ्गैः॒ संभृ॑तं वि॒श्वरू॑पम् ।
स उत् ति॑ष्ठे॒तो अ॒भि नाक॑मुत्त॒मं प॒द्भिश्च॒तुर्भिः॒ प्रति॑ तिष्ठ दि॒क्षु ॥
verses.transliteration:
śṛtamajaṃ śṛtayā prorṇuhi tvacā sarvairaṅgaiḥ saṃbhṛtaṃ viśvarūpam |
sa ut tiṣṭheto abhi nākamuttamaṃ padbhiścaturbhiḥ prati tiṣṭha dikṣu ||

verses.sanskrit:
स॒मुत्प॑तन्तु प्र॒दिशो॑ नभ॑स्वतीः॒ सम॒भ्राणि॒ वात॑जूतानि यन्तु ।
म॒ह॒ऋ॒ष॒भस्य॒ नद॑तो॒ नभ॑स्वतो वा॒श्रा आपः॑ पृथि॒वीं त॑र्पयन्तु ॥
verses.transliteration:
samutpatantu pradiśo nabhasvatīḥ samabhrāṇi vātajūtāni yantu |
mahaṛṣabhasya nadato nabhasvato vāśrā āpaḥ pṛthivīṃ tarpayantu ||
verses.translation:
A charm to hasten the coming of the rains
Let all the misty regions fly together, let all the rain-clouds sped by wind, assemble.
Let waters satisfy the earth, the voices of the great mist-enve-loped Bull who roareth.
Let them show forth, the strong, the bounteous Maruts: let plants and shrubs be hung with drops of moisture.
Let floods of rain refresh the ground with gladness and herbs spring various with each form and colour.
Cause us who sing to see the gathering vapours: out burst in many a place the rush of waters!
Let floods of rain refresh the ground with gladness; and herbs spring various with each form and colour.
Apart, Parjanya! let the troops of Maruts, roaring, swell the song.
Let pouring torrents of the rain that raineth rain upon the earth.
Up from the sea lift your dread might, ye Maruts: as light and splendour, send the vapour upward!
Let waters satisfy the earth, the voices of the great mist-enve-loped Bull who roareth.
Roar, thunder, set the sea in agitation, bedew the ground with thy sweet rain, Parjanya!
Send plenteous showers on him who seeketh shelter, and let the owner of lean kine go homeward.
Let the boon Maruts, let the springs and coiling serpents tend! you well.
Urged by the Maruts let the clouds pour down their rain upon. the earth.
Let lightning flash on every side: from all the regions blow the winds!
Urged by the Maruts let the clouds pour down their rain upon the earth.
May waters, lightning, cloud, and rain, boon springs and serpents tend you well.
Urged by the Maruts let the clouds pour down their rain upon the earth.
May he who hath become the plants’ high regent, suiting our bodies, Agni of the Waters,
May Jātavedas send us rain from heaven, Amrit and vital breath to earthly creatures.
Sending up waters from the flood and ocean Prajapati move the sea to agitation!
Forth flow the moisture of the vigorous stallion!
With this thy roar of thunder come thou hither,
Our father, Lord divine pouring the torrents. Let the streams breathe, O Varuna, of the waters.
Pour the floods down: along the brooks and channels let frogs with speckled arms send out their voices.
They who lay quiet for a year, the Brāhmans who fulfil their vows.
The frogs, have lifted up their voice, the voice Parjanya hath. inspired.
Speak forth a welcome, female frog! Do thou O frog, accost the rain.
Stretch thy four feet apart, and swim in the middle of the lake.
Khanvakhā, ho! Khaimakhā, ho! thou in the middle, Taduri!
Fathers, enjoy the rain from one who strives to win the Marutes heart.
Lift up the mighty cask and pour down water; let the wind blow, and lightnings flash around us.
Let sacrifice be paid, and, widely scattered, let herbs and plants be full of joy and gladness.

verses.sanskrit:
समी॑क्षयन्तु तवि॒षाः सु॒दान॑वो॒ ऽपां रसा॒ ओष॑धीभिः सचन्ताम् ।
व॒र्षस्य॒ सर्गा॑ महयन्तु॒ भूमिं॒ पृथ॑ग् जायन्ता॒मोष॑धयो वि॒श्वरू॑पाः ॥
verses.transliteration:
samīkṣayantu taviṣāḥ sudānavo 'pāṃ rasā oṣadhībhiḥ sacantām |
varṣasya sargā mahayantu bhūmiṃ pṛthag jāyantāmoṣadhayo viśvarūpāḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
समी॑क्षयस्व॒ गाय॑तो॒ नभां॑स्य॒पां वेगा॑सः॒ पृथ॒गुद् वि॑जन्ताम् ।
व॒र्षस्य॒ सर्गा॑ महयन्तु॒ भूमिं॑ पृथ॑ग् जायन्तां वी॒रुधो॑ वि॒श्वरू॑पाः ॥
verses.transliteration:
samīkṣayasva gāyato nabhāṃsyapāṃ vegāsaḥ pṛthagud vijantām |
varṣasya sargā mahayantu bhūmiṃ pṛthag jāyantāṃ vīrudho viśvarūpāḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
ग॒णास्त्वोप॑ गायन्तु॒ मारु॑ताः पर्जन्य घो॒षिणः॒ पृथ॑क् ।
सर्गा॑ व॒र्षस्य॒ वर्ष॑तो॒ वर्ष॑न्तु पृथि॒वीमनु॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
gaṇāstvopa gāyantu mārutāḥ parjanya ghoṣiṇaḥ pṛthak |
sargā varṣasya varṣato varṣantu pṛthivīmanu ||

verses.sanskrit:
उदी॑रयत मरुतः समुद्र॒तस्त्वे॒षो अ॒र्को नभ॒ उत् पा॑तयाथ ।
म॒ह॒ऋ॒ष॒भस्य॒ नद॑तो॒ नभ॑स्वतो वा॒श्रा आपः॑ पृथि॒वीं त॑र्पयन्तु ॥
verses.transliteration:
udīrayata marutaḥ samudratastveṣo arko nabha ut pātayātha |
mahaṛṣabhasya nadato nabhasvato vāśrā āpaḥ pṛthivīṃ tarpayantu ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒भि क्र॑न्द स्त॒नया॒र्दयो॑द॒धिं भूमिं॑ पर्जन्य॒ पय॑सा॒ सम॑ङ्धि ।
त्वया॑ सृ॒ष्टं ब॑हु॒लमैतु॑ व॒र्षमा॑शारै॒षी कृ॒शगु॑रे॒त्वस्त॑म् ॥
verses.transliteration:
abhi kranda stanayārdayodadhiṃ bhūmiṃ parjanya payasā samaṅdhi |
tvayā sṛṣṭaṃ bahulamaitu varṣamāśāraiṣī kṛśaguretvastam ||

verses.sanskrit:
सं वो॑ऽवन्तु सु॒दान॑व॒ उत्सा॑ अजग॒रा उ॒त ।
म॒रुद्भिः॒ प्रच्यु॑ता मे॒घा वर्ष॑न्तु पृथि॒वीमनु॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
saṃ vo'vantu sudānava utsā ajagarā uta |
marudbhiḥ pracyutā meghā varṣantu pṛthivīmanu ||

verses.sanskrit:
आशा॑माशां॒ वि द्यो॑ततां॒ वाता॑ वान्तु दि॒शोदि॑शः ।
म॒रुद्भिः॒ प्रच्यु॑ता मे॒घाः सं य॑न्तु पृथि॒वीमनु॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
āśāmāśāṃ vi dyotatāṃ vātā vāntu diśodiśaḥ |
marudbhiḥ pracyutā meghāḥ saṃ yantu pṛthivīmanu ||

verses.sanskrit:
आपो॑ वि॒द्युद॒भ्रं व॒र्षं सं वो॑ऽवन्तु सु॒दान॑व॒ उत्सा॑ अजग॒रा उ॒त ।
म॒रुद्भिः॒ प्रच्यु॑ता मे॒घाः प्राव॑न्तु पृथि॒वीमनु॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
āpo vidyudabhraṃ varṣaṃ saṃ vo'vantu sudānava utsā ajagarā uta |
marudbhiḥ pracyutā meghāḥ prāvantu pṛthivīmanu ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒पाम॒ग्निस्त॒नूभिः॑ संविदा॒नो य ओष॑धीनामधि॒पा ब॒भूव॑ ।
स नो॑ व॒र्षं व॑नुतां जा॒तवे॑दाः प्रा॒णं प्र॒जाभ्यो॑ अ॒मृतं॑ दि॒वस्परि॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
apāmagnistanūbhiḥ saṃvidāno ya oṣadhīnāmadhipā babhūva |
sa no varṣaṃ vanutāṃ jātavedāḥ prāṇaṃ prajābhyo amṛtaṃ divaspari ||

verses.sanskrit:
प्र॒जाप॑तिः सलि॒लादा स॑मुद्रादाप॑ ई॒रय॑न्नुद॒धिम॑र्दयाति ।
प्र प्या॑यतां॒ वृष्णो॒ अश्व॑स्य॒ रेतो॒ऽर्वाङे॒तेन॑ स्तनयि॒त्नुनेहि॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
prajāpatiḥ salilādā samudrādāpa īrayannudadhimardayāti |
pra pyāyatāṃ vṛṣṇo aśvasya reto'rvāṅetena stanayitnunehi ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒पो नि॑षि॒ञ्चन्नसु॑रः पि॒ता नः॒ श्वस॑न्तु॒ गर्ग॑रा अ॒पां व॑रु॒णाव॒ नीची॑र॒पः सृ॑ज ।
वद॑न्तु॒ पृश्नि॑बाहवो म॒ण्डूका॒ इरि॒णानु॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
apo niṣiñcannasuraḥ pitā naḥ śvasantu gargarā apāṃ varuṇāva nīcīrapaḥ sṛja |
vadantu pṛśnibāhavo maṇḍūkā iriṇānu ||

verses.sanskrit:
सं॒व॒त्स॒रं श॑शया॒ना ब्रा॑ह्म॒णा व्र॑तचा॒रिणः॑ ।
वाचं॑ प॒र्जन्य॑जिन्वितां॒ प्र म॒ण्डूका॑ अवादिषुः ॥
verses.transliteration:
saṃvatsaraṃ śaśayānā brāhmaṇā vratacāriṇaḥ |
vācaṃ parjanyajinvitāṃ pra maṇḍūkā avādiṣuḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
उ॒प॒प्रव॑द मण्डूकि व॒र्षमा व॑द तादुरि ।
मध्ये॑ ह्र॒दस्य॑ प्लवस्व वि॒गृह्य॑ च॒तुरः॑ प॒दः ॥
verses.transliteration:
upapravada maṇḍūki varṣamā vada tāduri |
madhye hradasya plavasva vigṛhya caturaḥ padaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
खण्व॒खा३इ॒ खैम॒खा३इ॒ मध्ये॑ तदुरि ।
व॒र्षं व॑नुध्वं पितरो म॒रुतां॒ मन॑ इछत ॥
verses.transliteration:
khaṇvakhāi khaimakhāi madhye taduri |
varṣaṃ vanudhvaṃ pitaro marutāṃ mana ichata ||

verses.sanskrit:
म॒हान्तं॒ कोश॒मुद॑चा॒भि षि॑ञ्च सविद्यु॒तं भ॑वतु॒ वातु॒ वातः॑ ।
त॒न्वतां॑ य॒ज्ञं ब॑हु॒धा विसृ॑ष्टा आन॒न्दिनी॒रोष॑धयो भवन्तु ॥
verses.transliteration:
mahāntaṃ kośamudacābhi ṣiñca savidyutaṃ bhavatu vātu vātaḥ |
tanvatāṃ yajñaṃ bahudhā visṛṣṭā ānandinīroṣadhayo bhavantu ||

verses.sanskrit:
बृ॒हन्ने॑षामधिष्ठा॒ता अ॑न्ति॒कादि॑व पश्यति ।
य स्ता॑यन्मन्य॑ते॒ चर॒न्त्सर्वं॑ दे॒वा इ॒दं वि॑दुः ॥
verses.transliteration:
bṛhanneṣāmadhiṣṭhātā antikādiva paśyati |
ya stāyanmanyate carantsarvaṃ devā idaṃ viduḥ ||
verses.translation:
On the omnipresence and omniscience of Varuna
The mighty Ruler of these worlds beholds as though from close at hand,
The man who thinks he acts by stealth: all this the Gods perceive and know.
If a man stands or walks or moves in secret, goes to his lying-down or his uprising,
What two men whisper as they sit together, King Varuna knows: he as the third is present.
This earth, too, is King Varuna’s possession, and the high heaven whose ends are far asunder.
The loins of Varuna are both the oceans, and this small drop of water, too, contains him.
If one should flee afar beyond the heaven, King Varuna would still be round about him.
Proceeding hither from the sky his envoys look, thousand-eyed, over the earth beneath them.
All this the royal Varuna beholdeth, all between heaven and earth and all beyond them.
The twinklings of men’s eyelids hath he counted. As one who plays throws dice he settles all things.
Those fatal snares of thine which stand extended, threefold,
O Varuna, seven by seven,
May they all catch the man who tells a falsehood, and pass un-harmed the man whose words are truthful.
Varuna, snare him with a hundred nooses! Man’s watcher! let not him who lies escape thee.
There let the villain sit with hanging belly and bandaged like a cask whose hoops are broken.
Varuna sends, and drives away, diseases: Varuna is both native and a stranger,
Varuna is celestial and is human.
I bind and hold thee fast with all these nooses, thou son of such a man and such a mother.
All these do I assign thee as thy portion.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्तिष्ठ॑ति॒ चर॑ति॒ यश्च॒ वञ्च॑ति॒ यो नि॒लायं॒ चर॑ति॒ यः प्र॒तङ्क॑म् ।
द्वौ सं॑नि॒षद्य॒ यन्म॒न्त्रये॑ते॒ राजा॒ तद् वे॑द॒ वरु॑णस्तृ॒तीयः॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
yastiṣṭhati carati yaśca vañcati yo nilāyaṃ carati yaḥ prataṅkam |
dvau saṃniṣadya yanmantrayete rājā tad veda varuṇastṛtīyaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
उ॒तेयं भूमि॒र्वरु॑णस्य॒ राज्ञ॑ उ॒तासौ द्यौर्बृ॑ह॒ती दू॒रेअ॑न्ता ।
उ॒तो स॑मु॒द्रौ वरु॑णस्य कु॒क्षी उ॒तास्मिन्नल्प॑ उद॒के निली॑नः ॥
verses.transliteration:
uteyaṃ bhūmirvaruṇasya rājña utāsau dyaurbṛhatī dūreantā |
uto samudrau varuṇasya kukṣī utāsminnalpa udake nilīnaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
उत यो द्याम॑ति॒सर्पा॑त् प॒रस्ता॒न्न स मु॑च्यातै॒ वरु॑णस्य॒ राज्ञः॑ ।
दि॒व स्पशः॒ प्र च॑रन्ती॒दम॑स्य सहस्रा॒क्षा अति॑ पश्यन्ति॒ भूमि॑म् ॥
verses.transliteration:
uta yo dyāmatisarpāt parastānna sa mucyātai varuṇasya rājñaḥ |
diva spaśaḥ pra carantīdamasya sahasrākṣā ati paśyanti bhūmim ||

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वं॒ तद् राजा॒ वरु॑णो॒ वि च॑ष्टे॒ यद॑न्त॒रा रोद॑सी॒ यत् प॒रस्ता॑त् ।
संख्या॑ता अस्य नि॒मिषो॒ जना॑नाम॒क्षानि॑व श्व॒घ्नी नि मि॑नोति॒ तानि॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
sarvaṃ tad rājā varuṇo vi caṣṭe yadantarā rodasī yat parastāt |
saṃkhyātā asya nimiṣo janānāmakṣāniva śvaghnī ni minoti tāni ||

verses.sanskrit:
ये ते॒ पाशा॑ वरुण स॒प्तस॑प्त त्रे॒धा तिष्ठ॑न्ति॒ विषि॑ता॒ रुश॑न्तः ।
छि॒नन्तु॒ सर्वे॒ अनृ॑तं॒ वद॑न्तं॒ यः स॑त्यवा॒द्यति॒ तं सृ॑जन्तु ॥
verses.transliteration:
ye te pāśā varuṇa saptasapta tredhā tiṣṭhanti viṣitā ruśantaḥ |
chinantu sarve anṛtaṃ vadantaṃ yaḥ satyavādyati taṃ sṛjantu ||

verses.sanskrit:
श॒तेन॒ पाशै॑र॒भि धे॑हि वरुणैनं॒ मा ते॑ मोच्यनृत॒वाङ् नृ॑चक्षः ।
आस्तां जा॒ल्म उ॒दरं॑ श्रंसयि॒त्वा कोश॑ इवाब॒न्धः प॑रिकृ॒त्यमा॑नः ॥
verses.transliteration:
śatena pāśairabhi dhehi varuṇainaṃ mā te mocyanṛtavāṅ nṛcakṣaḥ |
āstāṃ jālma udaraṃ śraṃsayitvā kośa ivābandhaḥ parikṛtyamānaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
यः स॑मा॒म्यो॒३वरु॑णो॒ यो व्या॒म्यो॒३यः सं॑दे॒श्यो॒३वरु॑णो॒ यो वि॑दे॒श्यः ।
यो दै॒वो वरु॑णो॒ यश्च॒ मानु॑षः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yaḥ samāmyovaruṇo yo vyāmyoyaḥ saṃdeśyovaruṇo yo videśyaḥ |
yo daivo varuṇo yaśca mānuṣaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
तैस्त्वा॒ सर्वै॑र॒भि ष्या॑मि॒ पाशै॑रसावामुष्यायणामुष्याः पुत्र ।
तानु॑ ते॒ सर्वा॑ननु॒संदि॑शामि ॥
verses.transliteration:
taistvā sarvairabhi ṣyāmi pāśairasāvāmuṣyāyaṇāmuṣyāḥ putra |
tānu te sarvānanusaṃdiśāmi ||

verses.sanskrit:
ईशा॑णां त्वा भेष॒जाना॒मुज्जे॑ष॒ आ र॑भामहे ।
च॒क्रे स॒हस्र॑वीर्यं॒ सर्व॑स्मा ओषधे त्वा ॥
verses.transliteration:
īśāṇāṃ tvā bheṣajānāmujjeṣa ā rabhāmahe |
cakre sahasravīryaṃ sarvasmā oṣadhe tvā ||
verses.translation:
A charm to secure freedom from various evils
We seize and hold thee, Conquering One! the queen of medi-cines that heal.
O Plant, I have endowed thee with a hundred powers for every man,
Still conquering, banishing the curse, mighty, with thy reverted. bloom.
Thee and all Plants have I invoked: Hence let it save us! was my prayer.
She who hath cursed us with a curse, or hath conceived a murderous sin,
Or seized our son to take his blood, may she devour the child she bare.
What magic they have wrought for thee in dish unbaked or burnt dark-red,
What they have wrought in flesh undressed,—conquer the sorcerers therewith.
Ill dream and wretchedness of life, Rākshasa, monster, stingy hags,
All the she-fiends of evil name and voice, we drive away from us.
Death caused by famine, caused by thirst, failure of children,. loss of kine,
With thee, O Apāmārga, all this ill we cleanse and wipe away.
Death caused by thirst, death caused by stress of hunger, loss at play with dice,
All this, O Apāmārga with thine aid we cleanse and wipe away.
The Apāmārga is alone the sovran of all Plants that grow.
With this we wipe away whate’er hath fallen on thee: go in health!

verses.sanskrit:
स॒त्य॒जितं॑ शपथ॒याव॑नीं॒ सह॑मानां पुनःस॒राम् ।
सर्वाः॒ सम॒ह्व्योष॑धीरि॒तो नः॑ पारया॒दिति॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
satyajitaṃ śapathayāvanīṃ sahamānāṃ punaḥsarām |
sarvāḥ samahvyoṣadhīrito naḥ pārayāditi ||

verses.sanskrit:
या श॒शाप॒ शप॑नेन॒ याघं मूर॑माद॒धे ।
या रस॑स्य॒ हर॑णाय जा॒तमा॑रे॒भे तो॒कम॑त्तु॒ सा ॥
verses.transliteration:
yā śaśāpa śapanena yāghaṃ mūramādadhe |
yā rasasya haraṇāya jātamārebhe tokamattu sā ||

verses.sanskrit:
यां ते॑ च॒क्रुरा॒मे पात्रे॒ यां च॒क्रुर्नी॑ललोहि॒ते ।
आ॒मे मां॒से कृ॒त्यां यां च॒क्रुस्तया॑ कृत्या॒कृतो॑ जहि ॥
verses.transliteration:
yāṃ te cakrurāme pātre yāṃ cakrurnīlalohite |
āme māṃse kṛtyāṃ yāṃ cakrustayā kṛtyākṛto jahi ||

verses.sanskrit:
दौष्व॑प्न्यं॒ दौर्जी॑वित्यं॒ रक्षो॑ अ॒भ्वऽमरा॒य्यः ।
दु॒र्णाम्नीः॒ सर्वा॑ दु॒र्वाच॒स्ता अ॒स्मन्ना॑शयामसि ॥
verses.transliteration:
dauṣvapnyaṃ daurjīvityaṃ rakṣo abhva'marāyyaḥ |
durṇāmnīḥ sarvā durvācastā asmannāśayāmasi ||

verses.sanskrit:
क्षु॒धा॒मा॒रं तृ॑ष्णामा॒रम॒गोता॑मनप॒त्यता॑म् ।
अपा॑मार्ग॒ त्वया॑ व॒यं सर्वं॒ तदप॑ मृज्महे ॥
verses.transliteration:
kṣudhāmāraṃ tṛṣṇāmāramagotāmanapatyatām |
apāmārga tvayā vayaṃ sarvaṃ tadapa mṛjmahe ||

verses.sanskrit:
तृ॒ष्णा॒मा॒रं क्षु॑धामा॒रमथो॑ अक्षपराज॒यम् ।
अपा॑मार्ग॒ त्वया॑ व॒यं सर्वं॒ तदप॒ मृज्महे ॥
verses.transliteration:
tṛṣṇāmāraṃ kṣudhāmāramatho akṣaparājayam |
apāmārga tvayā vayaṃ sarvaṃ tadapa mṛjmahe ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒पा॒मा॒र्ग ओष॑धीनां॒ सर्वा॑सा॒मेक॒ इद् व॒शी ।
तेन॑ ते मृज्म॒ आस्थि॑त॒मथ॒ त्वम॑ग॒दश्च॑र ॥
verses.transliteration:
apāmārga oṣadhīnāṃ sarvāsāmeka id vaśī |
tena te mṛjma āsthitamatha tvamagadaścara ||

verses.sanskrit:
स॒मं ज्योतिः॒ सूर्ये॒णाह्ना॒ रात्री॑ स॒मावती॑ ।
कृ॒णोमि॑ स॒त्यमू॒तये॑ऽर॒साः स॑न्तु॒ कृत्व॑रीः ॥
verses.transliteration:
samaṃ jyotiḥ sūryeṇāhnā rātrī samāvatī |
kṛṇomi satyamūtaye'rasāḥ santu kṛtvarīḥ ||
verses.translation:
A counter-charm against the incantations of enemies
The moonlight equalleth the sun, night is the rival of the day.
I make effectual power my help: let magic arts be impotent.
Gods! if one make and bring a spell on some man’s house who knows it not,
Close as the calf that sucks the cow may it revert and cling to him.
When one puts poison in a dish of unbaked clay to kill a man,
It cracks when set upon the fire with the sharp sound of many stones.
Endowed with thousand powers! adjure the bald and those with necks awry.
Back to its author turn the spell like a dear damsel to her friend!
I with this Plant have ruined all malignant powers of witchery.
The spell which they have laid upon thy field, thy cattle, or thy men.
No power had he who wrought the spell: he hurt his foot, he broke his toe.
His act hath brought us happiness and pain and sorrow to him-self.
Let Apāmārga sweep away chronic disease and every curse,
Sweep sorceresses clean away, and all malignant stingy hags.
Sweep thou away the sorcerers, all stingy fiendish hags away.
All this, O Apāmārga, with thine aid we wipe away from us.

verses.sanskrit:
यो दे॑वाः कृ॒त्यां कृ॒त्वा हरा॒दवि॑दुषो गृ॒हम् ।
व॒त्सो धा॒रुरि॑व मा॒तरं॒ तं प्र॒त्यगुप॑ पद्यताम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
yo devāḥ kṛtyāṃ kṛtvā harādaviduṣo gṛham |
vatso dhāruriva mātaraṃ taṃ pratyagupa padyatām ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒मा कृ॒त्वा पा॒प्मानं॒ यस्तेना॒न्यं जिघां॑सति ।
अश्मा॑न॒स्तस्यां॑ द॒ग्धायां॑ बहु॒लाः फट् क॑रिक्रति ॥
verses.transliteration:
amā kṛtvā pāpmānaṃ yastenānyaṃ jighāṃsati |
aśmānastasyāṃ dagdhāyāṃ bahulāḥ phaṭ karikrati ||

verses.sanskrit:
सह॑स्रधाम॒न् विशि॑खा॒न् विग्री॑वां छायया॒ त्वम् ।
प्रति॑ स्म च॒क्रुषे॑ कृ॒त्यां प्रि॒यां प्रि॒याव॑ते हर ॥
verses.transliteration:
sahasradhāman viśikhān vigrīvāṃ chāyayā tvam |
prati sma cakruṣe kṛtyāṃ priyāṃ priyāvate hara ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒नया॒हमोष॑ध्या सर्वाः॑ कृ॒त्या अ॑दूदुषम् ।
यां क्षेत्रे॑ च॒क्रुर्यां गोषु॒ यां वा॑ ते॒ पुरु॑षेषु ॥
verses.transliteration:
anayāhamoṣadhyā sarvāḥ kṛtyā adūduṣam |
yāṃ kṣetre cakruryāṃ goṣu yāṃ vā te puruṣeṣu ||

verses.sanskrit:
यश्च॒कार॒ न श॒शाक॒ कर्तुं॑ श॒श्रे पाद॑म॒ङ्गुरि॑म् ।
च॒कार॑ भ॒द्रम॒स्मभ्य॑मा॒त्मने॒ तप॑नं॒ तु सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yaścakāra na śaśāka kartuṃ śaśre pādamaṅgurim |
cakāra bhadramasmabhyamātmane tapanaṃ tu saḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒पा॒मा॒र्गोऽप॑ मार्ष्टु क्षेत्रि॒यं श॒पथ॑श्च॒ यः ।
अपाह॑ यातुधा॒नीरप॒ सर्वा॒ अरा॒य्यः ॥
verses.transliteration:
apāmārgo'pa mārṣṭu kṣetriyaṃ śapathaśca yaḥ |
apāha yātudhānīrapa sarvā arāyyaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒प॒मृज्य॑ यातु॒धाना॒नप॒ सर्वा॑ अरा॒य्यः ।
अपा॑मार्ग॒ त्वया॑ व॒यं सर्वं॒ तदप॒ मृज्महे ॥
verses.transliteration:
apamṛjya yātudhānānapa sarvā arāyyaḥ |
apāmārga tvayā vayaṃ sarvaṃ tadapa mṛjmahe ||

verses.sanskrit:
उ॒तो अ॒स्यब॑न्धुकृदु॒तो अ॑सि॒ नु जा॑मि॒कृत् ।
उ॒तो कृ॑त्या॒कृतः॑ प्र॒जां न॒डमि॒वा छि॑न्धि॒ वार्षि॑कम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
uto asyabandhukṛduto asi nu jāmikṛt |
uto kṛtyākṛtaḥ prajāṃ naḍamivā chindhi vārṣikam ||
verses.translation:
A counter-charm and charm to secure general protection.
Thou breakest ties of kith and kin, thou causest, too, relation-ship:
So bruise the sorcerer’s offspring, like a reed that groweth in the Rains.
Thou hast been blessed with blessing by the Brāhman, Kanva Nārshada.
Thou fliest like a flashing dart: there is no fear or danger, Plant! within the limit of thy range.
Illumining, as ‘twere, with light, thou movest at the head of plants.
The saviour of the simple man art thou, and slayer of the fiends.
As once when time began the Gods with thee expelled the Asuras,
Even thence, O Plant, wast thou produced as one who wipes and sweeps away.
Thy father’s name was Cleaver. Thou with thousand branches cleavest all.
Do thou, turned backward, cleave and rend the man who treateth us as foes.
The evil sprang from earth; it mounts to heaven and spreads to vast extent.
Reverted, shaking him with might, thence on its maker let it fall.
For thou hast grown reverted, and turned backward also is thy fruit.
Remove all curses far from me, keep most remote the stroke of death.
Preserve me with a hundred, yea, protect me with a thousand aids.
May mighty Indra, Lord of Plants! give store of strength and. power to thee.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रा॒ह्म॒णेन॒ पर्यु॑क्तासि॒ कण्वे॑न नार्ष॒देन॑ ।
सेने॑वैषि॒ त्विषी॑मती॒ न तत्र॑ भ॒यमस्ति॒ यत्र॑ प्रा॒प्नोष्यो॑षधे ॥
verses.transliteration:
brāhmaṇena paryuktāsi kaṇvena nārṣadena |
senevaiṣi tviṣīmatī na tatra bhayamasti yatra prāpnoṣyoṣadhe ||

verses.sanskrit:
अग्र॑मे॒ष्योष॑धीनां॒ ज्योति॑षेवाभिदी॒पय॑न् ।
उ॒त त्रा॒तासि॒ पाक॒स्याथो॑ ह॒न्तासि॑ र॒क्षसः॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
agrameṣyoṣadhīnāṃ jyotiṣevābhidīpayan |
uta trātāsi pākasyātho hantāsi rakṣasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
यद॒दो दे॒वा असु॑रां॒स्त्वयाग्रे॑ नि॒रकु॑र्वत ।
तत॒स्त्वमध्यो॑षधेऽपामा॒र्गो अ॑जायथाः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yadado devā asurāṃstvayāgre nirakurvata |
tatastvamadhyoṣadhe'pāmārgo ajāyathāḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
वि॒भि॒न्द॒ती श॒तशा॑खा विभि॒न्दन् नाम॑ ते पि॒ता ।
प्र॒त्यग् वि भि॑न्धि॒ त्वं तं यो अ॒स्माँ अ॑भि॒दास॑ति ॥
verses.transliteration:
vibhindatī śataśākhā vibhindan nāma te pitā |
pratyag vi bhindhi tvaṃ taṃ yo asmām̐ abhidāsati ||

verses.sanskrit:
अस॒द् भूम्याः॒ सम॑भव॒त् तद् यामे॑ति म॒हद् व्यचः॑ ।
तद् वै ततो॑ विधू॒पाय॑त् प्र॒त्यक् क॒र्तार॑मृच्छतु ॥
verses.transliteration:
asad bhūmyāḥ samabhavat tad yāmeti mahad vyacaḥ |
tad vai tato vidhūpāyat pratyak kartāramṛcchatu ||

verses.sanskrit:
प्र॒त्यङ् हि सं॑ब॒भूवि॑थ प्रती॒चीन॑फल॒स्त्वम् ।
सर्वा॒न् मच्छ॒पथाँ॒ अधि॒ वरी॑यो यावया व॒धम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
pratyaṅ hi saṃbabhūvitha pratīcīnaphalastvam |
sarvān macchapathām̐ adhi varīyo yāvayā vadham ||

verses.sanskrit:
श॒तेन॑ मा॒ परि॑ पाहि स॒हस्रे॑णा॒भि र॑क्ष मा ।
इन्द्र॑स्ते वीरुधां पत उ॒ग्र ओ॒ज्मान॒मा द॑धत् ॥
verses.transliteration:
śatena mā pari pāhi sahasreṇābhi rakṣa mā |
indraste vīrudhāṃ pata ugra ojmānamā dadhat ||

verses.sanskrit:
आ प॑श्यति॒ प्रति॑ पश्यति॒ परा॑ पश्यति॒ पश्य॑ति ।
दिव॑म॒न्तरि॑क्ष॒माद् भूमिं॒ सर्वं॒ तद् दे॑वि पश्यति ॥
verses.transliteration:
ā paśyati prati paśyati parā paśyati paśyati |
divamantarikṣamād bhūmiṃ sarvaṃ tad devi paśyati ||
verses.translation:
A charm for the acquisition of superhuman powers of sight
It sees in front, it sees behind, it sees afar away, it sees The sky, the firmament, and earth: all this, O Goddess, it beholds.
Through thee, O godlike Plant, may I behold all creatures that exist,
Three several heavens, three several earths, and these six regions one by one.
The pupil, verily, art thou of that celestial Engle’s eye.
On earth hast thou alighted as a weary woman seeks her couch.
The God who hath a thousand eyes give me this Plant in my right hand!
I look on every one therewith, each Sūdra and each Āryan man.
Make manifest the forms of things; hide not their essences from sight.
And, thou who hast a thousand eyes, look the Kimidins in the face.
Make me see Yātudhānas, make thou Yātudhānis visible.
Make me see all Pisāchas With this prayer, O Plant, I hold thee fast.
Thou art the sight of Kasyapa and of the hound who hath four eyes.
Make the Pisācha manifest as Sūrya when he rides at noon.
Kimidin, Yātudhāna from their hiding-places have I dragged.
I look on every one with this, Sūdra and Aryan man alike.
Make that Pisācha visible, the fiend who flies in middle air,
The fiend who glides across the sky, and him who deems the earth his help.

verses.sanskrit:
ति॒स्रो दिव॑स्ति॒स्रः पृ॑थि॒वीः षट् चे॒माः प्र॒दिशः॒ पृथ॑क् ।
त्वया॒हं सर्वा॑ भू॒तानि॒ पश्या॑नि देव्योषधे ॥
verses.transliteration:
tisro divastisraḥ pṛthivīḥ ṣaṭ cemāḥ pradiśaḥ pṛthak |
tvayāhaṃ sarvā bhūtāni paśyāni devyoṣadhe ||

verses.sanskrit:
दि॒व्यस्य॑ सुप॒र्णस्य॒ तस्य॑ हासि क॒नीनि॑का ।
सा भूमि॒मा रु॑रोहिथ व॒ह्यं श्रा॒न्ता व॒धूरि॑व ॥
verses.transliteration:
divyasya suparṇasya tasya hāsi kanīnikā |
sā bhūmimā rurohitha vahyaṃ śrāntā vadhūriva ||

verses.sanskrit:
तां मे॑ सहस्रा॒क्षो दे॒वो दक्षि॑णे॒ हस्त॒ आ द॑धत् ।
तया॒हं सर्वं॑ पश्यामि॒ यश्च॑ शू॒द्र उ॒तार्यः॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
tāṃ me sahasrākṣo devo dakṣiṇe hasta ā dadhat |
tayāhaṃ sarvaṃ paśyāmi yaśca śūdra utāryaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
आ॒विष्कृ॑णुष्व रू॒पाणि॒ मात्मान॒मप॑ गूहथाः ।
अथो॑ सहस्रचक्षो॒ त्वं प्रति॑ पश्याः किमी॒दिनः॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
āviṣkṛṇuṣva rūpāṇi mātmānamapa gūhathāḥ |
atho sahasracakṣo tvaṃ prati paśyāḥ kimīdinaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
द॒र्शय॑ मा यातु॒धाना॑न् द॒र्शय॑ यातुधा॒न्यः ।
पि॒शा॒चान्त्सर्वा॑न् दर्श॒येति॒ त्वा र॑भ ओषधे ॥
verses.transliteration:
darśaya mā yātudhānān darśaya yātudhānyaḥ |
piśācāntsarvān darśayeti tvā rabha oṣadhe ||

verses.sanskrit:
क॒श्यप॑स्य॒ चक्षु॑रसि शु॒न्याश्च॑ चतुर॒क्ष्याः ।
वी॒ध्रे सूर्य॑मिव॒ सर्प॑न्तं॒ मा पि॑शा॒चं ति॒र॒स्क॑रः ॥
verses.transliteration:
kaśyapasya cakṣurasi śunyāśca caturakṣyāḥ |
vīdhre sūryamiva sarpantaṃ mā piśācaṃ tiraskaraḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
उद॑ग्रभं परि॒पाणा॑द् यातु॒धानं॑ किमी॒दिन॑म् ।
तेना॒हं सर्वं॑ पश्याम्यु॒त शू॒द्रमु॒तार्य॑म् ॥
verses.transliteration:
udagrabhaṃ paripāṇād yātudhānaṃ kimīdinam |
tenāhaṃ sarvaṃ paśyāmyuta śūdramutāryam ||

verses.sanskrit:
यो अ॒न्तरि॑क्षेण॒ पत॑ति॒ दिवं॒ यश्चा॑ति॒सर्प॑ति ।
भूमिं॒ यो मन्य॑ते ना॒थं तं पि॑शा॒चं॑ प्र द॑र्शय ॥
verses.transliteration:
yo antarikṣeṇa patati divaṃ yaścātisarpati |
bhūmiṃ yo manyate nāthaṃ taṃ piśācaṃ pra darśaya ||

verses.sanskrit:
आ गावो॑ अग्मन्नु॒त भ॒द्रम॑क्र॒न्त्सीद॑न्तु गो॒ष्ठे र॒णय॑न्त्व॒स्मे ।
प्र॒जाव॑तीः पुरु॒रूपा॑ इ॒ह स्यु॒रिन्द्रा॑य पू॒र्वीरु॒षसो॒ दुहा॑नाः ॥
verses.transliteration:
ā gāvo agmannuta bhadramakrantsīdantu goṣṭhe raṇayantvasme |
prajāvatīḥ pururūpā iha syurindrāya pūrvīruṣaso duhānāḥ ||
verses.translation:
Glorification and benediction of cows
The kine have come and brought good fortune: let them rest in the cow-pen and be happy near us.
Here let them stay prolific, many-coloured, and yield through many morns their milk for Indra.
Indra aids him who offers sacrifice and praise: he takes not what is his, and gives him more thereto.
Increasing ever more and ever more his wealth, he makes the pious dwell within unbroken bounds.
These are ne’er lost, no robber ever injures them: no evil-minded foe attempts to harass them.
The master of the kine lives a long life with these, the Cows whereby he pours his gifts and serves the Gods.
The charger with his dusty brow o’ertakes them not, and never to the shambles do they take their way.
These Cows, the cattle of the pious worshipper, roam over wide-spread pasture where no danger is.
To me the Cows seem Bhaga, they seem Indra, they seem a portion of the first poured Soma.
These present Cows, they, O ye men, are Indra. I long for Indra with my heart and spirit.
O Cows, ye fatten e’en the worn and wasted, and make the unlovely beautiful to look on.
Prosper my home, ye with auspicious voices! Your power is magnified in our assemblies.
In goodly pasturage, bright-hued, prolific, drinking pure water at fair drinking-places,
Never be thief or sinful man your master, and may the dart of Rudra still avoid you!

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रो॒ यज्व॑ने गृण॒ते च॒ शिक्ष॑त॒ उपेद् द॑दाति॒ न स्वं मु॑षायति ।
भूयो॑भूयो र॒यिमिद॑स्य व॒र्धय॑न्नभि॒न्ने खि॒ल्ये नि द॑धाति देव॒युम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
indro yajvane gṛṇate ca śikṣata uped dadāti na svaṃ muṣāyati |
bhūyobhūyo rayimidasya vardhayannabhinne khilye ni dadhāti devayum ||

verses.sanskrit:
न ता न॑शन्ति॒ न द॑भाति॒ तस्क॑रो॒ नासा॑मामि॒त्रो व्य॒थिरा द॑धर्षति ।
दे॒वांश्च याभि॒र्यज॑ते॒ ददा॑ति च॒ ज्योगित् ताभिः॑ सचते॒ गोप॑तिः स॒ह ॥
verses.transliteration:
na tā naśanti na dabhāti taskaro nāsāmāmitro vyathirā dadharṣati |
devāṃśca yābhiryajate dadāti ca jyogit tābhiḥ sacate gopatiḥ saha ||

verses.sanskrit:
न ता अर्वा॑ रे॒णुक॑काटोऽश्नुते॒ न सं॑स्कृत॒त्रमुप॑ यन्ति॒ ता अ॒भि ।
उ॒रु॒गा॒यमभ॑यं॒ तस्य॒ ता अनु॒ गावो॒ मर्त॑स्य॒ वि च॑रन्ति॒ यज्व॑नः ॥
verses.transliteration:
na tā arvā reṇukakāṭo'śnute na saṃskṛtatramupa yanti tā abhi |
urugāyamabhayaṃ tasya tā anu gāvo martasya vi caranti yajvanaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
गावो॒ भगो॒ गाव॒ इन्द्रो॑ म इच्छा॒द् गावः॒ सोम॑स्य प्रथ॒मस्य॑ भ॒क्षः ।
इ॒मा या गावः॒ स ज॑नास॒ इन्द्र॑ इ॒च्छामि॑ हृ॒दा मन॑सा चि॒दिन्द्र॑म् ॥
verses.transliteration:
gāvo bhago gāva indro ma icchād gāvaḥ somasya prathamasya bhakṣaḥ |
imā yā gāvaḥ sa janāsa indra icchāmi hṛdā manasā cidindram ||

verses.sanskrit:
यू॒यं गा॑वो मेदयथ कृ॒शं चि॑दश्री॒रं चि॑त् कृणुथा सु॒प्रती॑कम् ।
भ॒द्रं गृ॒हं कृ॑णुथ भद्रवाचो बृ॒हद् वो॒ वय॑ उच्यते स॒भासु॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
yūyaṃ gāvo medayatha kṛśaṃ cidaśrīraṃ cit kṛṇuthā supratīkam |
bhadraṃ gṛhaṃ kṛṇutha bhadravāco bṛhad vo vaya ucyate sabhāsu ||

verses.sanskrit:
प्र॒जाव॑तीः सू॒यव॑से रु॒शन्तीः॑ शु॒द्धा अ॒पः सु॑प्रपा॒णे पिब॑न्तीः ।
मा व॑ स्ते॒न ई॑शत॒ माघशं॑सः॒ परि॑ वो रु॒द्रस्य॑ हे॒तिर्वृ॑णक्तु ॥
verses.transliteration:
prajāvatīḥ sūyavase ruśantīḥ śuddhā apaḥ suprapāṇe pibantīḥ |
mā va stena īśata māghaśaṃsaḥ pari vo rudrasya hetirvṛṇaktu ||

verses.sanskrit:
इ॒ममि॑न्द्र वर्धय क्ष॒त्रियं॑ म इ॒मं वि॒शामे॑क वृ॒षं कृ॑णु॒ त्वम् ।
निर॒मित्रा॑नक्ष्णुह्यस्य॒ सर्वां॒स्तान् र॑न्धयास्मा अहमुत्त॒रेषु॑ ॥
verses.transliteration:
imamindra vardhaya kṣatriyaṃ ma imaṃ viśāmeka vṛṣaṃ kṛṇu tvam |
niramitrānakṣṇuhyasya sarvāṃstān randhayāsmā ahamuttareṣu ||
verses.translation:
A benediction on a newly consecrated king
Exalt and strengthen this my Prince, O Indra, Make him sole lord and leader of the people.
Scatter his foes, deliver all his rivals into his hand in struggles for precedence.
Give him a share in village, kine, and horses, and leave his enemy without a portion.
Let him as King be head and chief of Princes, Give up to him,
O Indra, every foeman.
Let him be treasure-lord of goodly treasures, let him as King be master of the people.
Grant unto him great power and might, O Indra, and strip his enemy of strength and vigour.
Like milch-kine yielding milk for warm libations, pour, Heaven and Earth! on him full many a blessing.
May he as King be Indra’s well-beloved, the darling of the kine, the plants, the cattle.
I join in league with thee victorious Indra, with whom men conquer and are ne’er defeated.
He shall make thee the folk’s sole lord and leader, shall make thee highest of all human rulers.
Supreme art thou, beneath thee are thy rivals, and all, O King, who were thine adversaries.
Sole lord and leader and allied with Indra, bring, conqueror, thy foremen’s goods and treasures.
Consume, with lion aspect, all their hamlets, with tiger aspect, drive away thy foemen.
Sole lord and leader and allied with Indra, seize, conqueror, thine enemies’ possessions.

verses.sanskrit:
एमं भ॑ज॒ ग्रामे॒ अश्वे॑षु॒ गोषु॒ निष्टं भ॑ज॒ यो अ॒मित्रो॑ अ॒स्य ।
वर्ष्म॑ क्ष॒त्राणा॑म॒यम॑स्तु॒ राजेन्द्र॒ शत्रुं॑ रन्धय॒ सर्व॑म॒स्मै ॥
verses.transliteration:
emaṃ bhaja grāme aśveṣu goṣu niṣṭaṃ bhaja yo amitro asya |
varṣma kṣatrāṇāmayamastu rājendra śatruṃ randhaya sarvamasmai ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒यम॑स्तु धन॑पति॒र्धना॑नाम॒यं वि॒शां वि॒श्पति॑रस्तु॒ राजा॑ ।
अ॒स्मिन्नि॑न्द्र॒ महि॒ वर्चां॑सि धेह्यव॒र्चसं॑ कृणुहि॒ शत्रु॑मस्य ॥
verses.transliteration:
ayamastu dhanapatirdhanānāmayaṃ viśāṃ viśpatirastu rājā |
asminnindra mahi varcāṃsi dhehyavarcasaṃ kṛṇuhi śatrumasya ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒स्मै द्यावा॑पृथिवी॒ भूरि॑ वा॒मं दु॑हाथां घर्म॒दुघे॑ इव धे॒नू ।
अ॒यं राजा॒ प्रि॒य इन्द्र॑स्य भूयात् प्रि॒यो गवा॒मोष॑धीनां पशू॒नाम् ॥
verses.transliteration:
asmai dyāvāpṛthivī bhūri vāmaṃ duhāthāṃ gharmadughe iva dhenū |
ayaṃ rājā priya indrasya bhūyāt priyo gavāmoṣadhīnāṃ paśūnām ||

verses.sanskrit:
यु॒नज्मि॑ त उत्त॒राव॑न्त॒मिन्द्रं॒ येन॒ जय॑न्ति॒ न प॑रा॒जय॑न्ते ।
यस्त्वा॒ कर॑देकवृ॒षं जना॑नामु॒त राज्ञा॑मुत्तमं मा॑न॒वाना॑म् ॥
verses.transliteration:
yunajmi ta uttarāvantamindraṃ yena jayanti na parājayante |
yastvā karadekavṛṣaṃ janānāmuta rājñāmuttamaṃ mānavānām ||

verses.sanskrit:
उत्त॑र॒स्त्वमध॑रे ते स॒पत्ना॒ ये के च॑ राज॒न् प्रति॑शत्रवस्ते ।
ए॒क॒वृ॒ष इन्द्र॑सखा जिगी॒वां छ॑त्रूय॒तामा भ॑रा॒ भोज॑नानि ॥
verses.transliteration:
uttarastvamadhare te sapatnā ye ke ca rājan pratiśatravaste |
ekavṛṣa indrasakhā jigīvāṃ chatrūyatāmā bharā bhojanāni ||

verses.sanskrit:
सिं॒हप्र॑तीको॒ विशो॑ अद्धि॒ सर्वा॑ व्या॒घ्रप्र॑ती॒कोऽव॑ बाधस्व॒ शत्रू॑न् ।
ए॒क॒वृ॒ष इन्द्र॑सखा जिगी॒वां छ॑त्रूय॒तामा खि॑दा॒ भोज॑नानि ॥
verses.transliteration:
siṃhapratīko viśo addhi sarvā vyāghrapratīko'va bādhasva śatrūn |
ekavṛṣa indrasakhā jigīvāṃ chatrūyatāmā khidā bhojanāni ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒ग्नेर्म॑न्वे प्रथ॒मस्य॒ प्रचे॑तसः॒ पाञ्च॑जन्यस्य बहु॒धा यमि॒न्धते॑ ।
विशो॑ विशः प्रविशि॒वांस॑मीमहे॒ स नो मुञ्च॒त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
agnermanve prathamasya pracetasaḥ pāñcajanyasya bahudhā yamindhate |
viśo viśaḥ praviśivāṃsamīmahe sa no muñcatvaṃhasaḥ ||
verses.translation:
Magnification of Agni and prayer for his protection
I fix my heart on wise and ancient Agni, the Five Tribes’ Lord, in many a place enkindled.
We seek him who hath entered all our houses. May he deliver us from grief and trouble.
As thou conveyest offerings, Jātavedas! and fashionest the sacri-fice with knowledge,
So bear thou to the Gods the prayer we utter. May he deliver us from grief and trouble.
I pray to Agni in each act successful, employed in every sacrifice, the strongest,
Fiend-slayer, served with fatness, strengthening worship. May he deliver us from grief and trouble.
We invoke the oblation-bearer, well-born Agni Jātavedas,
Him, Vaisvānara, almighty. May he set us free from trouble.
With whom as friend the Rishis gave their power new splendour, with whom they kept aloof the Asuras’ devices,
Agni, with whom Indra subdued the Panis. May he deliver us. from grief and trouble.
Through whom the Gods discovered life eternal, through whom they stored the plants with pleasant juices,
Through whom they brought to men the light of heaven. May he deliver us from grief and trouble.
I, suppliant, praise and ever call on Agni, sole Lord of all this world, of all that shineth,
Of what exists and shall exist hereafter. May he deliver us from grief and trouble.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा॑ ह॒व्यं वह॑सि जातवेदो॒ यथा॑ य॒ज्ञं क॒ल्पय॑सि प्रजा॒नन् ।
ए॒वा दे॒वेभ्यः॑ सुम॒तिं न॒ आ व॑ह॒ स नो॑ मुञ्च॒त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yathā havyaṃ vahasi jātavedo yathā yajñaṃ kalpayasi prajānan |
evā devebhyaḥ sumatiṃ na ā vaha sa no muñcatvaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
याम॑न्याम॒न्नुप॑युक्तं॒ वहि॑ष्ठं॒ कर्म॑न्कर्म॒न्नाभ॑गम् ।
अ॒ग्निमी॑डे र॒क्षो॒हणं॑ यज्ञ॒वॄधं॑ घृ॒ताहु॑तं॒ स नो॑ मुञ्च॒त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yāmanyāmannupayuktaṃ vahiṣṭhaṃ karmankarmannābhagam |
agnimīḍe rakṣohaṇaṃ yajñavṝdhaṃ ghṛtāhutaṃ sa no muñcatvaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
सुजा॑तं जा॒तवे॑दसम॒ग्निं वै॑श्वान॒रं वि॒भुम् ।
ह॒व्य॒वाहं॑ हवामहे॒ स नो॑ मुञ्च॒त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
sujātaṃ jātavedasamagniṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vibhum |
havyavāhaṃ havāmahe sa no muñcatvaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
येन॒ ऋष॑यो ब॒लमद्यो॑तयन् यु॒जा येनासु॑राणा॒मयु॑वन्त मा॒याः ।
येना॒ग्निना॑ प॒णीनिन्द्रो॑ जि॒गाय॒ स नो॑ मुञ्च॒त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yena ṛṣayo balamadyotayan yujā yenāsurāṇāmayuvanta māyāḥ |
yenāgninā paṇīnindro jigāya sa no muñcatvaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
येन॑ दे॒वा अ॒मृत॑म॒न्ववि॑न्द॒न् येनौष॑धी॒र्मधु॑मती॒रकृण्वन् ।
येन॑ दे॒वाः स्व॑१राभ॑र॒न्त्स नो॑ मुञ्च॒त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yena devā amṛtamanvavindan yenauṣadhīrmadhumatīrakṛṇvan |
yena devāḥ svarābharantsa no muñcatvaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
यस्ये॒दं प्र॒दिशि॒ यद् वि॒रोच॑ते॒ यज्जा॒तं ज॑नित॒व्यंऽ च॒ केव॑लम् ।
स्तौम्य॒ग्निं ना॑थि॒तो जो॑हवीमि॒ स नो॑ मुञ्च॒त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yasyedaṃ pradiśi yad virocate yajjātaṃ janitavyaṃ' ca kevalam |
staumyagniṃ nāthito johavīmi sa no muñcatvaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्र॑स्य मन्महे॒ शश्व॒दिद॑स्य मन्महे वृत्र॒घ्न स्तोमा॒ उप॑ मे॒म आगुः॑ ।
यो दा॒शुषः॑ सु॒कृतो॒ हव॒मेति॒ स नो॑ मुञ्च॒त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
indrasya manmahe śaśvadidasya manmahe vṛtraghna stomā upa mema āguḥ |
yo dāśuṣaḥ sukṛto havameti sa no muñcatvaṃhasaḥ ||
verses.translation:
A hymn of prayer and praise to Indra
I think of Indra, only him for ever, fiend-slayer, May these lauds of mine come near him.
He cometh to the pious offerer’s calling. May he deliver us from grief and trouble.
Who with strong arms o’ercame his strong opponents, who broke and crushed the power of the demons,
Who won the rivers and the kine in battle. May he deliver us from grief and trouble.
Ruler of men, finder of light, the hero: the pressing-stones declare his valour, master.
Of sweetest sacrifice with seven Hotars. May he deliver us from grief and trouble.
The lord of barren cows and bulls and oxen, finder of light for whom the posts are planted,
For whom the bright juice flows cleansed by devotion. May he deliver us from grief and trouble.
Whose favour those desire who offer Soma, whom, arrow-bearer, men invoke in battle,
On whom the hymn depends, in whom is power, May he deliver us from grief and trouble.
Why was born, first, for active operation, whose valour as the first hath been awakened,
Who raised his bolt when he encountered Ahi. May he deliver us from grief and trouble.
Strong Lord, who leadeth hosts to meet for battle, who sendeth riches both of earth and heaven,
I, suppliant, praise and ever call on Indra. May he deliver us from grief and trouble.

verses.sanskrit:
य उ॒ग्रीणा॑मु॒ग्रबा॑हुर्य॒युर्यो दा॑न॒वानां॒ बल॑मारु॒रोज॑ ।
येन॑ जि॒ताः सिन्ध॑वो॒ येन॒ गावः॒ स नो॑ मुञ्च॒त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
ya ugrīṇāmugrabāhuryayuryo dānavānāṃ balamāruroja |
yena jitāḥ sindhavo yena gāvaḥ sa no muñcatvaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
यश्च॑र्षणि॒प्रो वृ॑ष॒भः स्व॒र्विद् यस्मै॒ ग्रावा॑णः प्र॒वद॑न्ति नृ॒म्णम् ।
यस्या॑ध्व॒रः स॒प्तहो॑ता॒ मदि॑ष्ठः॒ स नो॑ मुञ्च॒त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yaścarṣaṇipro vṛṣabhaḥ svarvid yasmai grāvāṇaḥ pravadanti nṛmṇam |
yasyādhvaraḥ saptahotā madiṣṭhaḥ sa no muñcatvaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य॑ व॒शास॑ ऋष॒भास॑ उ॒क्षणो॒ यस्मै॑ मी॒यन्ते॒ स्व॒र॑वः स्व॒र्विदे॑ ।
यस्मै॑ शु॒क्रः पव॑ते॒ ब्रह्म॑शुम्भितः॒ स नो॑ मुञ्च॒त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yasya vaśāsa ṛṣabhāsa ukṣaṇo yasmai mīyante svaravaḥ svarvide |
yasmai śukraḥ pavate brahmaśumbhitaḥ sa no muñcatvaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य॒ जुष्टिं॑ सो॒मिनः॑ का॒मय॑न्ते॒ यं हव॑न्त॒ इषु॑मन्तं॒ गवि॑ष्टौ ।
यस्मि॑न्न॒र्कः शि॑श्रि॒ये यस्मि॒न्नोजः॒ स नो॑ मुञ्च॒त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yasya juṣṭiṃ sominaḥ kāmayante yaṃ havanta iṣumantaṃ gaviṣṭau |
yasminnarkaḥ śiśriye yasminnojaḥ sa no muñcatvaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
यः प्र॑थ॒मः क॑र्म॒कृत्या॑य ज॒ज्ञे यस्य॑ वी॒र्यंऽ प्रथ॒मस्यानु॑बुद्धम् ।
येनोद्य॑तो॒ वज्रो॒ऽभ्याय॒ताहिं॒ स नो॑ मुञ्च॒त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yaḥ prathamaḥ karmakṛtyāya jajñe yasya vīryaṃ' prathamasyānubuddham |
yenodyato vajro'bhyāyatāhiṃ sa no muñcatvaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
यः सं॑ग्रा॒मान्नय॑ति॒ सं यु॒धे व॒शी यः पु॒ष्टानि॑ संसृ॒जति॑ द्व॒यानि॑ ।
स्तौमीन्द्रं॑ नाथि॒तो जो॑हवीमि॒ स नो॑ मुञ्च॒त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yaḥ saṃgrāmānnayati saṃ yudhe vaśī yaḥ puṣṭāni saṃsṛjati dvayāni |
staumīndraṃ nāthito johavīmi sa no muñcatvaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
वा॒योः स॑वि॒तुर्वि॒दथा॑नि मन्महे॒ यावा॑त्म॒न्वद् वि॒शथो॒ यौ च॒ रक्ष॑थः ।
यौ विश्व॑स्य परि॒भू ब॑भू॒वथु॒स्तौ नो॑ मुञ्चत॒मंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
vāyoḥ saviturvidathāni manmahe yāvātmanvad viśatho yau ca rakṣathaḥ |
yau viśvasya paribhū babhūvathustau no muñcatamaṃhasaḥ ||
verses.translation:
A hymn of prayer and praise to Vāyu and Savitar
I think on Vāyu’s and Savitar’s holy rites, ye twain who penetrate and guard the living world:
Ye who have come to be this All’s pervaders, deliver us, ye two from grief and trouble.
Ye who have counted up the earth’s expanses, and in the sky smoothed out the air’s midregion,
Whose going-forth hath ne’er been reached by any, deliver us, ye two, from grief and trouble.
Beauteously bright! men rest in thy dominion when thou hast risen up and hastened onward.
Ye, Vāyu, Savitar, preserve all creatures. Deliver us, ye, twain, from grief and trouble.
Hence, Vāyu, Savitar drive evil action, chase Simidā away, drive off the demons.
Ye give us store of energy and power. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.
Of their own selves let Savitar and Vāyu send favourable strength and wealth and plenty.
Here give us perfect freedom from consumption. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.
Ye, Savitar and Vāyu, to assist us, enjoy the hymn and the delightful cheerer.
Come hither downward from the stream of blessing. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.
Like noblest benisons they have stayed in the God loving man’s abode.
I glorify bright Savitar and Vāyu. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.

verses.sanskrit:
ययोः॒ संख्या॑ता॒ वरि॑मा॒ पार्थि॑वानि॒ याभ्यां॒ रजो॑ युपि॒तम॒न्तरि॑क्षे ।
ययोः॑ प्रा॒यं नान्वा॑न॒शे कश्च॒न तौ नो॑ मुञ्चत॒मंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yayoḥ saṃkhyātā varimā pārthivāni yābhyāṃ rajo yupitamantarikṣe |
yayoḥ prāyaṃ nānvānaśe kaścana tau no muñcatamaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
तव॑ व्र॒ते नि वि॑शन्ते॒ जना॑स॒स्त्वय्युदि॑ते॒ प्रेर॑ते चित्रभानो ।
यु॒वं वा॑यो सवि॒ता च॒ भुव॑नानि रक्षथ॒स्तौ नो॑ मुञ्चत॒मंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
tava vrate ni viśante janāsastvayyudite prerate citrabhāno |
yuvaṃ vāyo savitā ca bhuvanāni rakṣathastau no muñcatamaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
अपे॒तो वा॑यो सवि॒ता च॑ दुष्कृ॒तमप॒ रक्षां॑सि॒ शिमि॑दां च सेधतम् ।
सं ह्यू॒३र्जया॑ सृ॒जथः॒ सं बले॑न॒ तौ नो॑ मुञ्चत॒मंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
apeto vāyo savitā ca duṣkṛtamapa rakṣāṃsi śimidāṃ ca sedhatam |
saṃ hyūrjayā sṛjathaḥ saṃ balena tau no muñcatamaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
र॒यिं मे॒ पोषं॑ सवि॒तोत वा॒युस्त॒नू दक्ष॒मा सु॑वतां सु॒शेव॑म् ।
अ॒य॒क्ष्मता॑तिं॒ मह॑ इ॒ह ध॑त्तं॒ तौ नो॑ मुञ्चत॒मंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
rayiṃ me poṣaṃ savitota vāyustanū dakṣamā suvatāṃ suśevam |
ayakṣmatātiṃ maha iha dhattaṃ tau no muñcatamaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
प्र सु॑म॒तिं स॑वितर्वाय ऊ॒तये॒ मह॑स्वन्तं मत्स॒रं मा॑दयाथः ।
अ॒र्वाग् वा॒मस्य॑ प्र॒वतो॒ नि य॑च्छतं॒ तौ नो॑ मुञ्चत॒मंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
pra sumatiṃ savitarvāya ūtaye mahasvantaṃ matsaraṃ mādayāthaḥ |
arvāg vāmasya pravato ni yacchataṃ tau no muñcatamaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
उप॒ श्रेष्ठा॑ न आ॒शिषो॑ दे॒वयो॒र्धाम॑न्नस्थिरन् ।
स्तौमि॑ दे॒वं स॑वि॒तारं॑ च वा॒युं तौ नो॑ मुञ्चत॒मंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
upa śreṣṭhā na āśiṣo devayordhāmannasthiran |
staumi devaṃ savitāraṃ ca vāyuṃ tau no muñcatamaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
म॒न्वे वां॑ द्यावापृथिवी सुभोजसौ॒ सचे॑तसौ॒ ये अप्र॑थेथा॒ममि॑ता॒ योज॑नानि ।
प्र॒ति॒ष्ठे ह्यभ॑वतं॒ वसू॑नां॒ ते नो॑ मुञ्चत॒मंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
manve vāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī subhojasau sacetasau ye aprathethāmamitā yojanāni |
pratiṣṭhe hyabhavataṃ vasūnāṃ te no muñcatamaṃhasaḥ ||
verses.translation:
A hymn to Heaven and Earth
O Heaven and Earth, I think on you, wise, givers of abundant gifts, ye who through measureless expanses have spread forth.
For ye are seats and homes of goodly treasures. Deliver us, ye twain from grief and trouble.
Yea, seats and homes are ye of goodly treasures, grown strong, divine, blessed, and farextending,
To me, O Heaven and Earth, be ye auspicious. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.
I call on you who warm and cause no sorrow, deep, spacious, meet to be adored by poets.
To me, O Heaven and Earth, be ye auspicious. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.
Ye who maintain Amrit and sacrifices, ye who support rivers and human beings,
To me, O Heaven and Earth, be ye auspicious, Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.
Ye by whom cows and forest trees are cherished within whose range all creatures are included,
To me, O Heaven and Earth, be ye auspicious. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.
Ye who delight in nectar and in fatness, ye without whom men have no strength or power,
To me, O Heaven and Earth, be ye auspicious. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.
The grief that pains me here, whoever caused it, not sent by fate, hath sprung from human action.
I, suppliant, praise Heaven, Earth, and oft invoke them. Deliver us, ye twain, from grief and trouble.

verses.sanskrit:
प्र॒ति॒ष्ठे ह्यभ॑वत॒ वसू॑नां॒ प्रवृ॑द्धे देवी सुभगे उरूची ।
द्यावा॑पृथिवी॒ भव॑तं मे स्यो॒ने ते नो॑ मुञ्चत॒मंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
pratiṣṭhe hyabhavata vasūnāṃ pravṛddhe devī subhage urūcī |
dyāvāpṛthivī bhavataṃ me syone te no muñcatamaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
अ॒स॒न्ता॒पे सु॒तप॑सौ हुवे॒ऽहमु॒र्वी ग॑म्भी॒रे क॒विभि॑र्नम॒स्येऽ ।
द्यावा॑पृथिवी॒ भव॑तं मे स्यो॒ने ते नो॑ मुञ्चत॒मंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
asantāpe sutapasau huve'hamurvī gambhīre kavibhirnamasye' |
dyāvāpṛthivī bhavataṃ me syone te no muñcatamaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
ये अ॒मृतं॑ बिभृ॒थो ये ह॒वींषि॒ ये स्रो॒त्या बि॑भृ॒थो ये म॑नु॒ष्याऽन् ।
द्यावा॑पृथिवी॒ भव॑तं मे स्यो॒ने ते नो॑ मुञ्चत॒मंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
ye amṛtaṃ bibhṛtho ye havīṃṣi ye srotyā bibhṛtho ye manuṣyā'n |
dyāvāpṛthivī bhavataṃ me syone te no muñcatamaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
ये उ॒स्रिया॒ बिभृ॒थो ये वन॒स्पती॒न् ययो॑र्वां॒ विश्वा॒ भुव॑नान्य॒न्तः ।
द्यावा॑पृथिवी॒ भव॑तं मे स्यो॒ने ते नो॑ मुञ्चत॒मंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
ye usriyā bibhṛtho ye vanaspatīn yayorvāṃ viśvā bhuvanānyantaḥ |
dyāvāpṛthivī bhavataṃ me syone te no muñcatamaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
ये की॒लाले॑न त॒र्पय॑थो॒ ये घृ॒तेन॒ याभ्या॑मृ॒ते न किं च॒न श॑क्नु॒वन्ति ।
द्यावा॑पृथिवी॒ भव॑तं मे स्यो॒ने ते नो॑ मुञ्चत॒मंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
ye kīlālena tarpayatho ye ghṛtena yābhyāmṛte na kiṃ cana śaknuvanti |
dyāvāpṛthivī bhavataṃ me syone te no muñcatamaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
यन्मे॒दम॑भि॒शोच॑ति॒ येन॑येन वा कृ॒तं पौरु॑षेया॒न्न दैवा॑त् ।
स्तौमि॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी ना॑थि॒तो जो॑हवीमि॒ ते नो॑ मुञ्चत॒मंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
yanmedamabhiśocati yenayena vā kṛtaṃ pauruṣeyānna daivāt |
staumi dyāvāpṛthivī nāthito johavīmi te no muñcatamaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
म॒रुतां॑ मन्वे॒ अधि॑ मे ब्रुवन्तु॒ प्रेमं वाजं॒ वाज॑साते अवन्तु ।
आ॒शूनि॑व सु॒यमा॑नह्व ऊ॒तये॑ ते नो॑ मुञ्च॒न्त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
marutāṃ manve adhi me bruvantu premaṃ vājaṃ vājasāte avantu |
āśūniva suyamānahva ūtaye te no muñcantvaṃhasaḥ ||
verses.translation:
A hymn to the Maruts
I think upon the Maruts: may they bless me, may they assist me to this wealth in battle.
I call them like swift well-trained steeds to help us. May they deliver us from grief and trouble.
Those who surround the never-failing fountain for ever, and bedew the plants with moisture,
The Maruts, Prini’s sons, I chiefly honour. May they deliver us from grief and trouble.
Bards, who invigorate the milk of milch-kine, the sap of growing plants, the speed of coursers To us may the strong Maruts be auspicious. May they deliver us from grief and trouble.
They who raised water from the sea to heaven and send it from the sky to earth in showers,
The Maruts who move mighty with their waters, may they deliver us from grief and trouble.
They who delight in nectar and in fatness, they who bestow upon us health and vigour.
The Maruts who rain mighty with their waters, may they deliver us from grief and trouble.
Whether with stormy might the Maruts established this All, or Gods with their celestial power,
Ye, kindly Gods, are able to restore it. May they deliver us from grief and trouble.
Potent in battles is the Maruts’ army, impetuous train, well-known, exceeding mighty.
I, suppliant, praise and oft invoke the Maruts. May they deliver us from grief and trouble.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्स॒मक्षि॑तं॒ व्यच॑न्ति॒ ये सदा॒ य आ॑सि॒ञ्चन्ति॒ रस॒मोष॑धीषु ।
पु॒रो द॑धे मरुतः॒ पृश्नि॑मातृंस्ते नो॑ मुञ्च॒न्त्वंह॑सः ॥
verses.transliteration:
utsamakṣitaṃ vyacanti ye sadā ya āsiñcanti rasamoṣadhīṣu |
puro dadhe marutaḥ pṛśnimātṛṃste no muñcantvaṃhasaḥ ||

verses.sanskrit:
पयो॑ धेनू॒नां रस॒मोष॑धीनां ज॒वमर्व॑तां कवयो॒ य इन्व॑थ ।
